notes: Canonical ruleset the pipeline reads. Generated from the raw pull; do not hand-edit — edit in Airtable and re-run build_ruleset.py.
thresholds_status from Airtable (Draft/Calibrated/Not Applicable). Numbers in measurable_signal are RECOMMENDATIONS, not rules, until a row is Calibrated. No verdicts are produced here.
judge/proxy_only/skip derived from measurable_by_pose. pose_landmarks tokens validated against CONTROLLED_VOCAB (landmark_derivations.py).
phase / phase_order (where present) name the phase a measurement belongs to and its position in the required sequence — the order is itself coached.

records.name: WR - Catching - Away - Chest/Mid - Extend & Bait
records.ideal_execution_standard: Hold the running trajectory and snap the eyes toward the incoming ball, judging its lateral path while keeping stride length intact. Fire BOTH arms outward away from the torso into the lateral lane, torquing the upper chest slightly toward the ball without breaking the lower body's running line, and form a tight diamond out wide with thumbs and index fingers connected and palms squared to the side-angle trajectory.
records.fault_trigger: REACHING WITH ONE HAND - extending only the leading arm, cutting the catching surface in half. Also: the hips rotating with the chest, which breaks the running line and costs stride. (Hand shape needs the Hand landmarker.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Lateral extension distance of both wrists away from Sternum, resolved in the image plane perpendicular to the running heading, expressed in torso lengths - maximum reach to the catch side. Plus BOTH wrists extending together (a single extended wrist is the one-hand fault). Plus partial shoulder-line rotation toward the catch side WITHOUT the hip line following - the lower body must hold its running line. Plus thumb and index convergence forming the diamond. NOTE: hand shape needs the HAND LANDMARKER; extension, torque and stride continuity are measurable today.
records.coaching_cue: Two hands out wide - turn your chest, not your feet.

records.name: WR - Catching - Away - Chest/Mid - The Strike
records.ideal_execution_standard: Intercept the nose of the ball out wide in the centre of the diamond, elbows unlocked to absorb the high-velocity lateral momentum. The nose must be pointed exactly at the hands at the moment of impact - not tracking the ball peripherally.
records.fault_trigger: THE PERIPHERAL PEEK - trying to catch using only peripheral vision with the nose pointed straight downfield, which ruins hand-eye coordination and depth perception. THE STIFF LATERAL LOCKOUT - catching out wide with locked elbows, so the ball clanks off rigid fingertips.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] TWO signals at the impact frame. (1) LATERAL TRACKING: head YAW (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) must rotate fully to the catch side so the Nose vector points at the laterally-extended wrist midpoint. A Nose still pointing downfield while the hands are out wide is THE PERIPHERAL PEEK fault - measured as the angular gap between head direction and wrist midpoint at impact. (2) ELBOW GIVE: elbow flexion increasing across the frames immediately after contact rather than staying locked. NOTE: this is a YAW measurement, unlike the centre catches which measure pitch. Fingertip vs palm contact also needs the Hand landmarker; the ball itself needs object detection.
records.coaching_cue: Point your nose at your hands - don't catch it out the corner of your eye.

records.name: WR - Catching - Away - Chest/Mid - The Tuck
records.ideal_execution_standard: Sweep the ball back tightly across the body into the core ribcage, instantly snapping the chin down and across the torso to visually lock the ball into the tuck position before looking upfield.
records.fault_trigger: The head snapping back downfield while the ball is still being swept across the body, so the rotational momentum of the sweep pulls the eyes off the leather and the ball is lost mid-transfer.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] LATERAL NOSE-TO-THE-TUCK METRIC - fully measurable from pose today, no Hand landmarker required. Track the lateral retraction of the wrist midpoint sweeping back across the torso toward Sternum, and simultaneously track head YAW. The head must sweep inward MATCHING THE SPEED of the returning wrists - measured as the correlation between the two curves plus any frame offset. The specific risk here is that the rotational momentum of the sweep rips the eyes off the ball, so any yaw that outruns or lags the wrists is the fault. Plus wrist-to-Sternum distance closing to near zero.
records.coaching_cue: Sweep it in and let your chin ride with it.

records.name: WR - Catching - Away - High - Extend & Bait
records.ideal_execution_standard: Track the high, fading trajectory and time the jump or upper-body extension to meet the ball out wide at its highest point. Shoot both arms violently upward and outward on a 45-degree diagonal with elbows slightly flexed, hands open wide with thumbs locked together and index fingers pointing diagonally upward to form the overhead triangle.
records.fault_trigger: TURNING PINKIES UP - reaching up and out with the pinkies together, which turns the palms completely away from the ball's path. THE OVERHEAD CLAP - slapping the hands together laterally from the sides instead of clamping the ball's incoming line. (Hand orientation needs the Hand landmarker.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] DIAGONAL extension of both wrists - combining vertical elevation above the shoulder line AND lateral displacement away from Sternum, resolved in the image plane, expressed in torso lengths. The measurement is the resultant diagonal reach, target roughly 45 degrees up and out. Plus elbow flexion (slightly flexed, not locked), shoulder-midpoint elevation showing the shrug up and out, and THUMB convergence with index fingers pointing diagonally up. NOTE: thumbs-together vs pinkies-up detection needs the HAND LANDMARKER.
records.coaching_cue: Up and out at 45 - thumbs locked.

records.name: WR - Catching - Away - High - The Strike
records.ideal_execution_standard: Pluck the ball out of the air at its highest possible lateral apex, staring directly through the diagonal window formed by the hands. The head must not drift back toward the centre of the body before the ball is secured.
records.fault_trigger: THE EARLY CENTRE DROP - catching the ball diagonally but snapping the head back to the centre of the field before pulling it down, leading to a blind tuck and a high chance of dropping it on turf impact.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] COMBINED PITCH AND YAW TRACKING at the impact frame - the only catch in the set requiring both simultaneously. The Nose vector must be pitched UPWARD and rotated LATERALLY so it intersects the high-diagonal wrist midpoint. Measured as the angular gap between head direction and wrist midpoint in both axes. The head drifting back toward the body's centre line before the hands close is the fault, and it is detected as yaw returning toward the running heading while the wrists are still out wide. Plus vertical wrist height peaking at or immediately before impact, not after. NOTE: fingertip wrap and the ball itself need the Hand landmarker and object detection.
records.coaching_cue: Stare through the diagonal window - don't drift back to centre.

records.name: WR - Catching - Away - High - The Tuck
records.ideal_execution_standard: Pull the ball down violently across the chest, rolling the head diagonally downward to visually track the ball all the way from the high-outside quadrant into chest protection as the feet return to the turf.
records.fault_trigger: The head returning to centre or upfield before the ball reaches the chest, completing the tuck blind - the most common way a spectacular high-and-wide catch becomes a drop on landing.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] DIAGONAL NOSE-TO-THE-TUCK METRIC - fully measurable from pose today. Track the wrist midpoint retracting on a diagonal (downward AND inward across the chest) toward Sternum, and simultaneously track BOTH Nose pitch and yaw. The head must follow that same diagonal path - measured as correlation between head direction and wrist position in both axes across the retraction frames, plus frame offset. This is the most demanding tracking case in the catalogue: the head must rotate on two axes at once while the body is landing. Plus knee flexion increasing on landing.
records.coaching_cue: Rip it down across your chest - eyes ride it all the way.

records.name: WR - Catching - Away - Low - Extend & Bait
records.ideal_execution_standard: Track the low, diving path and drop the entire body level by bending deeply at the knees and hips. Drop both arms diagonally downward toward the grass on the catch side with elbows tucked near the lower ribcage, inverting the hands out to the side - pinky fingers pressed tightly together, palms facing upward and outward - to form a secure under-scoop.
records.fault_trigger: WAIST-BENDING REACHES - keeping the legs straight and bending sideways at the waist, which destroys balance and pulls the eyes away from the ball. THUMBS-TOGETHER LOW CATCH - trying to scoop a low-lateral ball with the thumbs together, forcing the palms to face the ground. (Hand inversion needs the Hand landmarker.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Vertical drop of Pelvis Center and bilateral knee flexion, expressed in torso lengths. CRITICALLY, cross-check the Spine vector against the hip-to-knee vector AND the shoulder-line tilt to distinguish a knee-and-hip sink from WAIST-BENDING SIDEWAYS: hips staying high while the torso folds laterally is the fault. Plus wrists dropping BOTH downward and laterally (diagonal drop toward the grass on the catch side), elbows tucked near the lower ribcage, and PINKY convergence with palms up and out. NOTE: no pinky landmark exists in the 33-point pose model - inverted-hand detection needs the HAND LANDMARKER.
records.coaching_cue: Sink and reach - bend your knees, not your waist.

records.name: WR - Catching - Away - Low - The Strike
records.ideal_execution_standard: Slide the inverted hands underneath the dipping path of the ball, with the chin tucked to the catch-side shoulder and the eyes glued to the grass-level pinky basket as the ball settles in.
records.fault_trigger: Eyes lifting off the basket before the fingers close. On a low-and-wide catch the hands are at their furthest from the head, so peripheral tracking is at its least reliable and the margin is smallest.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] COMBINED PITCH AND YAW TRACKING at the impact frame - the Nose vector must be pitched STEEPLY DOWNWARD and rotated LATERALLY (chin toward the catch-side shoulder), intersecting the low-and-wide wrist midpoint. Measured as the angular gap between head direction and wrist midpoint in both axes. Plus wrist height held below the hip line, and the wrist pair positioned UNDER the ball's incoming path rather than beside it. NOTE: fingertip angle and the curl need the Hand landmarker; the ball needs object detection.
records.coaching_cue: Chin to your shoulder - eyes glued to the basket.

records.name: WR - Catching - Away - Low - The Tuck
records.ideal_execution_standard: Roll the hands and forearms upward and across the stomach, keeping the head down and rotated laterally. Watch the ball leave the lateral plane and physically touch the stomach before the eyes snap up to run.
records.fault_trigger: THE UP-AND-OUT PULL - catching the ball low and wide but immediately pulling the head up and away to look at a defender, so the ball slips out of the pinkies during the lateral sweep. The longest, least secure transfer of any catch in the set.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] LOW-LATERAL NOSE-TO-THE-TUCK METRIC - fully measurable from pose today, and the hardest case in the catalogue. Track the wrist midpoint rolling UPWARD and sweeping INWARD across the stomach toward Sternum, while simultaneously tracking Nose pitch and yaw. The head must stay locked in the low-lateral quadrant, following the wrists through the entire sweep, with ZERO upfield yaw until wrist-to-Sternum distance reaches near zero. Measured as the angular gap in both axes across every retraction frame, plus the exact frame at which any upfield rotation begins relative to the frame the wrists reach the torso.
records.coaching_cue: Watch it touch your gut before you look up.

records.name: WR - Catching - Center - Chest/Mid - Extend & Bait
records.ideal_execution_standard: Hold a strong base with the eyes locked on the point of the ball. Shoot the arms forward away from the jersey to meet the ball early and maximise the catching radius, forming a tight symmetric diamond with thumbs and index fingers pressed together and palms turned outward to face the incoming ball.
records.fault_trigger: BODY CATCHING - letting the ball travel all the way into the chest pads instead of extending the hands, so it bounces off hard plastic armour and results in drops or deflections. (Hand shape needs the Hand landmarker.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Horizontal extension distance of both wrists away from Sternum at the catch approach, expressed in torso lengths - maximum reach, with the wrists clearly forward of the chest plane rather than resting against it. Plus elbow flexion angle (relaxed, not locked). Plus convergence of the thumbs and index fingers into a diamond. NOTE: thumb and index points exist in the 33-point pose model but are LOW FIDELITY; reliable diamond-shape detection needs the HAND LANDMARKER. Wrist proximity and orientation give a usable proxy until then.
records.coaching_cue: Catch it out front - never off the pads.

records.name: WR - Catching - Center - Chest/Mid - The Strike
records.ideal_execution_standard: Let the nose of the ball enter the centre of the diamond while the eyes stay hyper-focused on the leather. The elbows stay relaxed and flexible to give with the ball and absorb its force, with the fingertips - not the palms - clamping the panels.
records.fault_trigger: THE EARLY LOOK - snapping the head up to look at an oncoming defender right before the ball hits the hands, causing a ricochet off the fingertips. THE STIFF-ARM CLANK - catching with locked-out elbows and hard palms; without joint elasticity a fast ball clanks off the hands. (Ball contact needs object detection.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] TWO signals at the impact frame. (1) TRACKING: the Nose vector must point at the midpoint between the left and right wrists at the exact frame of impact - measured as the angular difference between head direction and the wrist midpoint. Any deviation (head snapping up or away) is THE EARLY LOOK fault. (2) ELBOW GIVE: elbow flexion angle must INCREASE across the frames immediately after contact, showing the arms absorbing rather than resisting. Elbow angle staying flat or locked is the stiff-arm fault. NOTE: fingertip vs palm contact needs the Hand landmarker; the ball itself needs object detection.
records.coaching_cue: Eyes on the leather - let the elbows give.

records.name: WR - Catching - Center - Chest/Mid - The Tuck
records.ideal_execution_standard: Pull the ball tightly back into the ribcage, wrapping the arm completely over it for a four-point pressure hold. Instantly drop the chin to visually confirm the catch - nose to the tuck - before snapping the eyes upfield to look for defenders.
records.fault_trigger: Eyes leaving the ball before the tuck is complete - the head comes up to find defenders while the ball is still being secured, which is how a clean catch becomes a fumble. Also: no chin drop at all, so the catch is never visually confirmed.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] THE NOSE-TO-THE-TUCK METRIC - fully measurable from pose today, no Hand landmarker required. Track the vertical descent of the wrist midpoint as it retracts toward Sternum, and simultaneously track Nose pitch (Nose relative to the ear midpoint). The head must pitch DOWNWARD in step with the descending wrists - measured as the correlation between the two across the retraction frames, plus any frame offset between them. A Nose vector that stops following the wrists, or yaws away upfield, before the wrists reach Sternum is the fault. Plus wrist-to-Sternum distance closing to near zero (the tuck) and elbow wrapping over.
records.coaching_cue: Nose to the tuck - chin follows it in before you run.

records.name: WR - Catching - Center - High - Extend & Bait
records.ideal_execution_standard: Track the high trajectory and time the jump or extension so the hands intercept the ball at the absolute apex of reach. Shoot both arms violently upward above the forehead with elbows slightly flexed, hands open wide with thumbs pressed tightly together and index fingers pointing up, creating an inverted triangle to look through.
records.fault_trigger: TURNING PINKIES OUT - reaching up for a high ball with the pinkies together instead of the thumbs. This turns the palms away from the ball and makes a clean high catch impossible. (Hand orientation needs the Hand landmarker.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Vertical elevation of both wrists relative to the shoulder line, expressed in torso lengths - maximum reach, wrists clearly above forehead height. Plus elbow flexion angle (slightly flexed, not locked out), and shoulder-midpoint elevation showing the shrug toward the ears. Plus convergence of the THUMBS with index fingers pointing upward, forming the window. NOTE: reliable thumbs-together vs pinkies-together detection needs the HAND LANDMARKER - this distinction is the defining difference between a high and a low catch and the 33-point pose model cannot resolve it reliably.
records.coaching_cue: Thumbs together, reach through the roof.

records.name: WR - Catching - Center - High - The Strike
records.ideal_execution_standard: Stare directly through the window created by the hands and pluck the ball out of the air at its highest possible point, fingers spread wide and thumbs facing each other right before impact, fingertips wrapping tightly around the tip and sides to halt its momentum mid-air.
records.fault_trigger: THE BLIND PULL - tilting the head back down toward the turf before the hands secure the ball, resulting in a blind, clapping attempt at the apex. CLAPPING AT THE BALL - slapping the hands together from the sides; if the timing is off by a millisecond the palms hit the ball and knock it away.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] TWO signals at the impact frame. (1) TRACKING: Nose pitched UPWARD (Nose relative to the ear midpoint), with the head vector pointing at the midpoint between the elevated wrists - the receiver is looking through the thumb window. Head pitching back down toward the turf before the wrists close is THE BLIND PULL fault. (2) APEX: vertical height of the wrist midpoint should reach its maximum at or immediately before the impact frame, not after - a peak occurring late means the receiver caught it on the way down rather than at the top. NOTE: fingertip wrap and the ball itself need the Hand landmarker and object detection.
records.coaching_cue: Look through the window - pluck it at the top.

records.name: WR - Catching - Center - High - The Tuck
records.ideal_execution_standard: Pull the ball down violently to the chest as the feet return to the turf, the head snapping down to follow the ball's descent from the sky straight into the core, then immediately roll the body or shoulders over the ball to protect it from closing defenders.
records.fault_trigger: Head staying tilted up after the catch rather than following the ball down into the body, so the tuck is never visually confirmed. Also: landing stiff-legged without knee flexion, costing balance and the ability to run after the catch.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] THE NOSE-TO-THE-TUCK METRIC, high-catch variant - fully measurable from pose today. Track the rapid vertical descent of the wrist midpoint from overhead down to Sternum, and simultaneously track Nose pitch. The head must pitch downward MIRRORING THE SPEED of the descending wrists - measured as the correlation between the two curves and any frame offset. Plus bilateral knee flexion increasing on landing (absorbing ground impact), and shoulder rotation over the ball afterwards. A head that stops following the wrists before they reach Sternum is the fault.
records.coaching_cue: Rip it down and follow it with your chin.

records.name: WR - Catching - Center - Low - Extend & Bait
records.ideal_execution_standard: Track the downward trajectory and lower the entire body frame by bending at the knees and hips rather than folding at the waist. Drop the arms toward the grass with elbows tucked close to the torso, then invert the hands completely - pinky fingers pressed together, palms facing upward - creating a clean scoop to cradle the dipping ball.
records.fault_trigger: BENDING AT THE WAIST - keeping the legs straight and simply leaning over. This ruins balance, alters eye level dramatically, and prevents running after the catch. THUMBS-UP MISTAKE - trying to catch a low ball with the thumbs together like a chest catch, forcing the hands upside down so the ball slips straight through onto the ground. (Hand inversion needs the Hand landmarker.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Vertical drop of Pelvis Center and bilateral knee flexion, expressed in torso lengths - the whole frame must lower. CRITICALLY, cross-check the Spine vector angle (Pelvis Center to Sternum) against the hip-to-knee vector to distinguish a knee-and-hip sink from BENDING AT THE WAIST: if the hips stay high while the torso folds forward, that is the fault. Plus wrists dropping low with elbows tucked close to the torso, and PINKY convergence with palms up. NOTE: there is NO pinky landmark in the 33-point pose model - inverted-hand detection needs the HAND LANDMARKER. Body lowering is fully measurable today.
records.coaching_cue: Sink your base - pinkies together, palms up.

records.name: WR - Catching - Center - Low - The Strike
records.ideal_execution_standard: Keep the eyes hyper-focused on the hands and slide the inverted basket underneath the path of the ball, fingertips angled slightly upward right before impact, letting the ball land smoothly into the pinky basket while the fingers instantly curl around the leather.
records.fault_trigger: EARLY EYES - snapping the head up to look at the defence while the ball is still inches from the pinkies, causing it to slip through the arms onto the grass. On a low catch there is no margin: the eyes must stay down until the fingers close.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] TRACKING: Nose pitched STEEPLY DOWNWARD (Nose relative to the ear midpoint), with the head vector pointing at the low wrist midpoint across the frames before and at impact. The head must stay locked in the lower quadrant - any upward pitch or yaw away before the hands close is the EARLY EYES fault. Plus wrist height staying below the hip line, and the wrist pair positioned UNDER the incoming path rather than in front of it. NOTE: fingertip angle and the curl around the leather need the Hand landmarker; the ball needs object detection.
records.coaching_cue: Eyes down in the basket - get under it.

records.name: WR - Catching - Center - Low - The Tuck
records.ideal_execution_standard: Roll the hands and forearms upward toward the stomach, cradling the ball securely against the body frame so it cannot slip out. The eyes stay locked on the ball as it transitions from the grass line up into the stomach - do not look up to run yet.
records.fault_trigger: Looking up to run before the ball is rolled securely into the abdomen. The low catch is the least secure of all four, so any early upfield glance during the roll-up is how the ball ends up on the grass.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] THE NOSE-TO-THE-TUCK METRIC, low-catch variant - fully measurable from pose today. Track the upward roll of the wrist midpoint from the grass line toward Sternum, and simultaneously track Nose pitch. The Nose vector must stay locked on the wrists through the entire roll-up, with ZERO yaw upfield until the wrists reach Sternum. Measured as the angular difference between head direction and wrist midpoint across every frame of the retraction, plus the frame at which any upfield yaw begins. Plus elbow flexion increasing as the forearms cradle in.
records.coaching_cue: Roll it up to your gut - don't look up yet.

records.name: WR - Catching - Over the Shoulder - Extend & Bait
records.ideal_execution_standard: Sprint at top speed along the route track with a steady, bounce-free head. Keep the hands down and relaxed while running, extending the arms upward only at the absolute last second to keep the trailing defender blind, then raise the hands near collarbone or chin level with pinkies pressed together and palms open to the sky, forming a deep running basket.
records.fault_trigger: REACHING EARLY - running downfield with the arms extended to the sky for ten yards. This alerts the defender to play the arms, slows top sprint speed, and makes tracking the ball far harder. (Basket formation needs the Hand landmarker.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] TWO signals. (1) LATE EXTENSION: vertical height of both wrists relative to Sternum held at normal sprint-pump level, with elevation occurring only in the final frames before the catch. The FRAME at which the wrists rise is the measurement - sustained elevation earlier is the REACHING EARLY fault. (2) SPRINT CONTINUITY: forward velocity of Pelvis Center and stride cadence held constant across the extension - no stutter or break in stride. Plus PINKY convergence with palms open to the sky at collarbone level. NOTE: there is NO pinky landmark in the 33-point pose model - basket formation and palm orientation need the HAND LANDMARKER.
records.coaching_cue: Hands down late - then build the bucket.

records.name: WR - Catching - Over the Shoulder - The Strike
records.ideal_execution_standard: The eyes track the nose of the ball dropping from the sky straight down into the open palms. The wrists stay completely loose and cushioned right before impact, letting the ball melt into the fingers without disrupting the running stride.
records.fault_trigger: PEEKING - letting the head drift back forward toward the end zone just before the ball drops into the bucket, so it hits the helmet or falls straight through the hands. THE PALMS-FORWARD BARRIER - facing the palms toward the line of scrimmage instead of up to the sky, creating a wall the ball bounces off rather than a basket it falls into.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] TWO signals at the impact frame. (1) HEAD ROTATION HELD: head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) maintaining a strict rotational angle back over the shoulder, with the head vector pointing at the wrist midpoint. Any forward yaw back toward the end zone before the wrists close is the PEEKING fault, and it is measured as the frame at which that yaw begins. (2) WRIST CUSHION: wrist angle staying loose, with a small downward give at contact rather than a rigid barrier. NOTE: palm orientation (up to the sky vs forward) is the defining feature here and needs the HAND LANDMARKER; head rotation and sprint continuity are measurable today.
records.coaching_cue: Palms to the sky - don't peek forward.

records.name: WR - Catching - Over the Shoulder - The Tuck
records.ideal_execution_standard: Clamp the fingers around the ball the instant it settles into the hands, pulling it straight down into the pocket arm position while the head stays rotated over the shoulder and the eyes stay locked on the hands until the ball is safely into the chest - all without breaking the vertical sprint into the end zone.
records.fault_trigger: Snapping the head forward before the ball is secured into the chest pocket, so the catch is completed blind. Also: breaking stride or stuttering during the tuck, which surrenders the separation the route created.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] THE NOSE-TO-THE-TUCK METRIC, over-the-shoulder variant - fully measurable from pose today. Track the wrist midpoint retracting down and back into the chest pocket, and simultaneously track head yaw. The head must hold its rotation over the shoulder with ZERO forward yaw until the wrists make contact with the torso - the measurement is the frame offset between wrist-torso contact and the onset of forward head rotation. A head that snaps forward first is the fault. Plus sprint cadence and Pelvis Center velocity holding through the tuck, with no stutter or break in stride.
records.coaching_cue: Squeeze it, look it in, keep running.

records.name: WR - First Steps - 1 Step - Arm Drive
records.ideal_execution_standard: Arms drive in rhythm with the legs - opposite arm to opposite leg - with the elbows held at a consistent working angle to add drive out of the stance.
records.fault_trigger: Arms out of sync with the legs, arms crossing the body's midline rather than driving forward and back, or elbows flailing/locking so the arms add no drive.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Elbow flexion angle from the Shoulder-Elbow-Wrist vectors, and contralateral timing: the opposite arm and leg reaching maximum forward extension within the same frame window.

records.name: WR - First Steps - 1 Step - Base Width
records.ideal_execution_standard: Feet stay under the body through the first steps - narrow enough to run efficiently, wide enough to stay balanced through the acceleration.
records.fault_trigger: Base widening through the first steps, costing efficiency and drive; or narrowing so far the receiver crosses over and loses balance.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Lateral distance between the ankles at each ground contact, expressed in shoulder widths (L-R Shoulder as the scale unit) so it stays size-independent.

records.name: WR - First Steps - 1 Step - Body Lean
records.ideal_execution_standard: The torso leans forward through the initial acceleration, driving the body out of the stance. The lean comes from the whole body angled forward, not from bending at the waist.
records.fault_trigger: Standing straight up out of the stance, killing acceleration; or bending at the waist so the chest folds forward ahead of the hips instead of the whole body leaning.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Angle of the torso vector (hip midpoint to shoulder midpoint) relative to vertical across the acceleration phase. Cross-check against the hip-to-knee vector to distinguish a whole-body lean from waist flexion.

records.name: WR - First Steps - 1 Step - First Step Direction
records.ideal_execution_standard: The first step travels directly along the intended release heading, without lateral drift that costs ground or telegraphs the release direction.
records.fault_trigger: First step drifting laterally off the release heading, widening the path and costing ground before the route develops.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Angle of the first step's ankle displacement relative to the intended release heading, measured in the image plane. Lateral drift is the deviation from that heading.

records.name: WR - First Steps - 1 Step - First Step Length
records.ideal_execution_standard: The first step is short and driving rather than long and reaching - it establishes ground contact quickly and underneath the body so the second step can build speed.
records.fault_trigger: Overstriding on the first step so the foot lands ahead of the body's mass and brakes rather than drives; or a step so short it fails to create separation.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Distance between the stance-planted foot and the first-step foot at ground contact, expressed in shoulder widths (L-R Shoulder as the scale unit) so it stays size-independent. Cross-check landing ankle position relative to Pelvis Center - landing ahead of the hips indicates braking.

records.name: WR - First Steps - 1 Step - Front-Foot Roll-Off
records.ideal_execution_standard: The receiver rolls off the front foot into the release - the heel lifts while the toe stays in contact, driving the body forward. The roll-off leads the forward travel rather than following it.
records.fault_trigger: Backward weight transfer before the roll-off, the whole foot leaving the ground flat rather than rolling through the toe, or excessive vertical rise instead of forward drive.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Vertical rise of the front heel relative to its own Foot Index (heel lifting while the toe stays down), timed against the onset of forward Pelvis Center velocity. Correct order is heel lift LEADING forward travel.

records.name: WR - First Steps - 1 Step - Ground Contact
records.ideal_execution_standard: Ground contact is short and driving - the foot strikes underneath the body and leaves quickly, adding speed rather than absorbing it.
records.fault_trigger: Long ground contact times, or the foot striking ahead of the body with backward velocity - braking on each step instead of driving.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Frames between foot-strike and toe-off per step (ground contact time), plus horizontal ankle velocity at strike - negative velocity relative to the release heading indicates braking.

records.name: WR - First Steps - 1 Step - Head / Eyes
records.ideal_execution_standard: Head transitions from the inside snap cue to the release path and defensive target, turning under control without whipping or dropping.
records.fault_trigger: Head whipping round or dropping during the release, or failing to transition from the ball to the release path. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Head yaw from Nose position relative to the ear midpoint, compared against the shoulder line, tracked across the release. NOTE: orientation only - actual EYE GAZE is not measurable from the 33-point pose model. Whether the head starts oriented at the BALL needs ball tracking; which side is 'inside' needs the alignment side.

records.name: WR - First Steps - 1 Step - Hip Alignment
records.ideal_execution_standard: Hips stay driving toward the release heading through the first steps, opening only as far as the release path requires.
records.fault_trigger: Hips over-rotating off the release heading, widening the path and costing ground; or staying square when the release requires them to turn.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Angle of the hip line (L-R Hip vector) relative to the release heading, tracked across the first steps. NOTE: measured against the release heading, since the line of scrimmage is not determinable from a solo clip.

records.name: WR - First Steps - 1 Step - Pad Level
records.ideal_execution_standard: Pads stay low out of the stance and rise gradually across the first steps as speed builds, rather than popping upright immediately.
records.fault_trigger: Shoulders spiking upright on the first step rather than rising gradually, losing the forward drive angle and slowing acceleration.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Vertical height of the shoulder midpoint expressed in torso lengths, and its rate of rise across the first three steps. Gradual rise is correct; a step-change (spiking upright) is the fault.

records.name: WR - First Steps - 1 Step - Release Path
records.ideal_execution_standard: The body travels on a consistent, committed path off the line, matching the angle the called release requires - inside or outside - without drifting or rounding.
records.fault_trigger: Drifting or rounding off the line rather than committing to a release angle. (Whether the angle matches the called release needs the route to be declared - not determinable from a solo clip.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Angle of the Pelvis Center trajectory across the first three steps relative to the stance facing. NOTE: whether this matches the CALLED release (inside vs outside) needs the route to be declared - report the measured angle, do not judge it.

records.name: WR - First Steps - 1 Step - Shoulder Alignment
records.ideal_execution_standard: Shoulders stay connected to the hips and square to the release path, moving with the lower body rather than rotating independently of it.
records.fault_trigger: Shoulders rotating away from the hips and the release path, disconnecting upper and lower body and telegraphing the release direction.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Angle between the shoulder line and the hip line (separation), plus shoulder-line angle relative to the release path, tracked across the first steps.

records.name: WR - First Steps - 1 Step - Stance-to-Step Transition
records.ideal_execution_standard: The first movement travels forward along the release heading. No backward or lateral step is taken before the release begins - the receiver goes directly from the loaded stance into the first step.
records.fault_trigger: A false step - a backward or sideways step before the first forward step - losing ground and time before the route begins.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Displacement of the first moving ankle between the stance frame and its first ground contact, resolved along the release heading in the image plane. Negative displacement along that axis indicates a false step. Cross-check Pelvis Center displacement over the same window. NOTE: resolved in the image plane against the release heading, not via MediaPipe Z, which is unreliable monocular.

records.name: WR - First Steps - 1 Step - Weight Transfer
records.ideal_execution_standard: Weight moves continuously forward through the first three steps, staying ahead of the base of support so each step drives rather than catches.
records.fault_trigger: Weight stalling or moving backward relative to the feet, so a step catches the body instead of driving it forward.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Horizontal position of Pelvis Center relative to the base of support (the ankle pair), tracked across the first three steps. Continuous forward progression is correct.

records.name: WR - First Steps - 5 Yards - Acceleration Rate
records.ideal_execution_standard: Speed builds continuously across the first 5 yards - each step adds velocity, with no early plateau or stall in the acceleration.
records.fault_trigger: Velocity plateauing early in the 5 yards, or stalling between steps - the receiver reaches a speed and stops building rather than accelerating through the stem. (Absolute rate needs a scale reference.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Rate of change of Pelvis Center velocity across the 5-yard distance. Continuous positive acceleration without early velocity plateaus. NOTE: absolute units require a scale reference (player height) - without it, report the acceleration PROFILE (shape and continuity) rather than an absolute figure.

records.name: WR - First Steps - 5 Yards - Arm Drive & Contralateral Timing
records.ideal_execution_standard: Arms drive front-to-back in rhythm with the legs - opposite arm to opposite leg - at a consistent elbow angle, without swinging across the body.
records.fault_trigger: Arms out of sync with the legs, swinging across the body's midline rather than driving front-to-back, or elbows flailing and locking so the arms add no drive.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Elbow flexion angle from the Shoulder-Elbow-Wrist vectors, plus contralateral timing: opposite arm and leg reaching peak forward extension within the same frame window. Also check wrist horizontal position relative to Sternum - crossing the body's midline indicates transverse swing.

records.name: WR - First Steps - 5 Yards - Base Width Progression
records.ideal_execution_standard: The base starts wider through the driving first steps, then narrows progressively into a linear running track by the fifth yard as the receiver transitions from acceleration to running.
records.fault_trigger: Base staying wide through the whole 5 yards, costing efficiency and speed; or narrowing too early so the driving steps lose their power base.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Lateral distance between the ankles at each ground contact, expressed in shoulder widths (L-R Shoulder as the scale unit). Expect a TRANSITION from a wider acceleration base at Steps 1-2 to a narrow, linear running track by Yard 5 - the measurement is the narrowing trend, not any single contact.

records.name: WR - First Steps - 5 Yards - First Step Direction
records.ideal_execution_standard: The first step travels directly along the intended release heading, without lateral drift that costs ground or telegraphs the release direction.
records.fault_trigger: First step drifting laterally off the release heading, widening the path and costing ground before the stem develops.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Angle of the first step's ankle displacement relative to the intended release heading, measured in the image plane. Lateral drift is the deviation from that heading.

records.name: WR - First Steps - 5 Yards - First Step Length
records.ideal_execution_standard: The first step is short and driving rather than long and reaching - it establishes ground contact quickly and underneath the body so the following steps can expand.
records.fault_trigger: Overstriding on the first step so the foot lands ahead of the body's mass and brakes rather than drives; or a step so short it fails to create separation.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Distance between the stance-planted foot and the first-step foot at ground contact, expressed in shoulder widths (L-R Shoulder as the scale unit) so it stays size-independent. Cross-check landing ankle position relative to Pelvis Center - landing ahead of the hips indicates braking.

records.name: WR - First Steps - 5 Yards - Foot Strike / Braking Elimination
records.ideal_execution_standard: Each foot lands under or slightly behind the hips during the acceleration steps, so every strike drives the body forward instead of braking it.
records.fault_trigger: Foot landing ahead of the hips at strike, creating a braking force that costs speed on every step - typically caused by overstriding out of the stance.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Horizontal position of the landing ankle relative to Pelvis Center at each touchdown. Landing under or slightly behind Pelvis Center during the early steps prevents negative horizontal (braking) velocity at strike. Cross-check ankle horizontal velocity at strike - negative relative to the heading is braking.

records.name: WR - First Steps - 5 Yards - Front-Foot Roll-Off
records.ideal_execution_standard: The receiver rolls off the front foot into the drive - the heel lifts while the toe stays in contact, driving the body forward. The roll-off leads the forward travel rather than following it.
records.fault_trigger: Backward weight transfer before the roll-off, the whole foot leaving the ground flat rather than rolling through the toe, or excessive vertical rise instead of forward drive.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Vertical rise of the front heel relative to its own Foot Index (heel lifting while the toe stays down), timed against the onset of forward Pelvis Center velocity. Correct order is heel lift LEADING forward travel.

records.name: WR - First Steps - 5 Yards - Ground Contact Time Decay
records.ideal_execution_standard: Ground contact shortens progressively across the 5 yards - longer on the driving first steps, then quicker as speed builds and the receiver transitions to running.
records.fault_trigger: Ground contact times staying flat or lengthening across the 5 yards - the receiver is not converting drive into speed, and each step absorbs rather than adds velocity.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Frames between foot-strike and toe-off per step across the 5 yards. Ground contact time must DECREASE progressively as running speed increases - the measurement is the decay curve, not any single contact.

records.name: WR - First Steps - 5 Yards - Head / Eyes Stability
records.ideal_execution_standard: The head stays stable and level through the 5-yard drive, held steady enough to read the defender's leverage and cushion while the body accelerates.
records.fault_trigger: Head bobbing, whipping or dropping through the drive, so the receiver cannot process the defender's leverage. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation and stability only.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Head yaw from Nose position relative to the ear midpoint, compared against the shoulder line, tracked across the 5-yard drive; plus yaw variance as a stability measure. NOTE: orientation only - actual EYE GAZE is not measurable from the 33-point pose model, so whether the receiver is reading coverage leverage cannot be confirmed.

records.name: WR - First Steps - 5 Yards - Pad Level & Rise Rate
records.ideal_execution_standard: Pads stay low out of the stance and rise smoothly and gradually across the 5 yards as speed builds, reaching upright running posture only once the acceleration phase is complete.
records.fault_trigger: Popping upright prematurely rather than rising gradually, losing the forward drive angle and cutting acceleration short.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Vertical height of the shoulder midpoint expressed in torso lengths, and the SLOPE of its rise across the 5 yards. A smooth, gradual, near-linear rise is correct; a step-change (popping upright) is the fault.

records.name: WR - First Steps - 5 Yards - Rotational Economy
records.ideal_execution_standard: The torso stays quiet through the acceleration - shoulders and hips rotate only as much as the stride requires, so energy goes into forward drive rather than twisting.
records.fault_trigger: Excessive torso rotation during max-effort strides - the shoulders counter-rotating hard against the hips, wasting energy that should go into forward drive.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Angle between the shoulder line and the hip line (rotational separation) during max-effort acceleration strides, tracked across the 5 yards. Excessive or growing separation indicates energy lost to torso rotation rather than forward drive.

records.name: WR - First Steps - 5 Yards - Stance-to-Step Transition
records.ideal_execution_standard: The first movement travels forward along the release heading. No backward or lateral step is taken before the drive begins - the receiver goes directly from the loaded stance into the first step.
records.fault_trigger: A false step - a backward or sideways step before the first forward step - losing ground and time before the stem begins.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Displacement of the first moving ankle between the stance frame and its first ground contact, resolved along the release heading in the image plane. Negative displacement indicates a false step. Cross-check Pelvis Center displacement over the same window. NOTE: resolved in the image plane against the release heading, not via MediaPipe Z, which is unreliable monocular.

records.name: WR - First Steps - 5 Yards - Stem Directional Drift
records.ideal_execution_standard: The stem holds a straight, committed line across the 5 yards - the body travels on the intended heading without drifting laterally, so the route develops on time and the break happens where it should.
records.fault_trigger: Drifting laterally off the stem heading across the 5 yards, changing the depth and angle at which the break occurs. (Whether the heading matches the called route needs the route to be declared.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Lateral deviation of the Pelvis Center trajectory relative to the intended stem heading across the 5 yards, resolved in the image plane. NOTE: resolved against the stem heading rather than a raw image axis, and not via MediaPipe Z, which is unreliable monocular. Whether the stem heading itself is correct needs the route to be declared.

records.name: WR - First Steps - 5 Yards - Stride Length Progression
records.ideal_execution_standard: Stride length expands progressively across the first 5 yards - short and driving at Step 1, opening up as speed builds through Steps 4 and 5.
records.fault_trigger: Strides not expanding - staying short and choppy through the whole 5 yards; or opening up too early, overstriding out of the stance before speed supports it.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Distance between successive foot-strikes expressed in shoulder widths (L-R Shoulder as the scale unit). Stride length must EXPAND progressively from Step 1 through Steps 4-5 - the measurement is the progression, not any single stride.

records.name: WR - First Steps - 5 Yards - Torso Drive Angle / Body Lean
records.ideal_execution_standard: The torso holds an aggressive forward drive angle through the early steps - roughly 45 to 60 degrees from vertical - then transitions smoothly upfield as speed builds. The angle comes from the whole body driving forward, not from bending at the waist.
records.fault_trigger: Standing too upright out of the stance, killing the drive angle; bending at the waist so the chest folds ahead of the hips; or holding the forward angle too long and failing to transition upfield.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Angle of the torso vector (Pelvis Center to shoulder midpoint) relative to vertical across the acceleration phase. Reference range 45-60 degrees through the early steps, transitioning smoothly upright. Cross-check against the hip-to-knee vector to distinguish a whole-body drive angle from waist flexion. NOTE: the 45-60 range is an uncalibrated starting reference, not a rule.

records.name: WR - First Steps - 5 Yards - Weight Transfer Progression
records.ideal_execution_standard: Weight moves continuously forward across the full 5 yards, staying ahead of the base of support so every step drives rather than catches.
records.fault_trigger: Weight stalling or falling back behind the feet at any point in the 5 yards, so a step catches the body instead of driving it forward.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Horizontal position of Pelvis Center relative to the base of support (the ankle pair), tracked across the full 5 yards to confirm continuous forward progression rather than only the opening steps.

records.name: WR - First Steps - Blocking - Approach / Closing Velocity
records.ideal_execution_standard: The receiver closes the cushion under control - accelerating to eat up ground, then gathering before contact rather than running through the block at full speed.
records.fault_trigger: Over-running the block - arriving at full speed with no gather, so the receiver loses balance on contact and the defender sheds him easily. (Cushion distance needs the defender in frame.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Forward velocity of Pelvis Center along the blocking trajectory, and its rate of change across the approach - controlled acceleration followed by deceleration into contact, not a flat sprint. NOTE: the defender is NOT in frame in a solo clip, so cushion distance cannot be measured; only the receiver's own velocity profile is assessable.

records.name: WR - First Steps - Blocking - Centre of Mass Drop
records.ideal_execution_standard: The hips drop into a loaded athletic squat before contact, establishing low leverage so the receiver arrives underneath the defender rather than upright.
records.fault_trigger: Arriving tall and only sinking at or after contact, so the defender gets underneath the receiver's pads and uprights him immediately.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Vertical height of Pelvis Center across the approach, expressed in torso lengths, and the timing of its drop relative to the final steps. The drop should occur BEFORE contact, not at it.

records.name: WR - First Steps - Blocking - First Step Power Stagger
records.ideal_execution_standard: The first step is short, controlled and punchy, planting underneath the body's mass so power is available immediately rather than reaching out and losing the base.
records.fault_trigger: Overstriding on the first step so the foot lands ahead of the body's mass, which kills the power base and leaves the receiver reaching rather than driving.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Length of the first step along the blocking trajectory, expressed in shoulder widths (L-R Shoulder as the scale unit). Cross-check the landing ankle position relative to Pelvis Center - the foot should plant under the body's mass, not ahead of it.

records.name: WR - First Steps - Blocking - Hand Extension & Shoot Velocity
records.ideal_execution_standard: The hands shoot forward violently at engagement, extending fast into the defender's chest frame rather than arriving late or short.
records.fault_trigger: Slow or short hand extension, so the receiver makes contact with his chest rather than his hands and has no control of the defender. (Hand placement on the defender needs them in frame; grip needs the Hand landmarker.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Forward velocity of the wrists and their extension distance from the shoulders along the target vector, at the engagement frame. The measurement is the speed and reach of the punch. NOTE: whether the hands land INSIDE THE DEFENDER'S CHEST FRAME needs the defender in frame; hand placement relative to the receiver's own body is measurable. Grip and finger detail needs the Hand landmarker.

records.name: WR - First Steps - Blocking - Head Up / Target Eye Alignment
records.ideal_execution_standard: The head stays up with the eyes on the target through contact - the receiver sees what he is blocking rather than ducking his head into the collision.
records.fault_trigger: Dipping or ducking the head before contact - the receiver loses sight of the target and cannot adjust, and it is an unsafe way to take a collision. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Head pitch angle (Nose relative to the ear midpoint) measured against the torso vector, tracked through the approach and at contact - the head must stay up, with no downward dip or duck before impact. NOTE: orientation only - actual EYE GAZE is not measurable from the 33-point pose model.

records.name: WR - First Steps - Blocking - Hip Drive at Engagement
records.ideal_execution_standard: The hips extend hard as the hands make contact, driving ground force up through the torso and into the defender so the block has power behind it rather than just reach.
records.fault_trigger: Hands landing without hip extension behind them - an arms-only block with no ground force, which the defender sheds easily. Or the hips firing before the hands arrive, wasting the drive.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Rate of extension of the hip angle (Shoulder-Hip-Knee vector) at the frame the hands make contact. The measurement is the hip extension firing IN TIME with the hand contact, transferring ground force through the torso into the block.

records.name: WR - First Steps - Blocking - Knee Flexion / Power Angle
records.ideal_execution_standard: The knees hold a strong power angle - roughly 90 to 120 degrees - approaching and through impact, absorbing the collision and providing the platform to drive.
records.fault_trigger: Knees straightening into contact, leaving the receiver stiff-legged with nothing to absorb the collision or drive through it; or collapsing so deep he cannot move his feet.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Bilateral knee flexion angles from the Hip-Knee-Ankle vectors, held across the approach and through impact. Reference range 90-120 degrees. NOTE: this range is an uncalibrated starting reference, not a rule.

records.name: WR - First Steps - Blocking - Lateral Alignment / Tracking
records.ideal_execution_standard: The receiver tracks a consistent line onto the defender, staying square to them so they cannot slip past inside or outside before the hands fit.
records.fault_trigger: Drifting off the tracking line during the approach, so the defender slips past inside or outside before contact is made. (Alignment to the defender needs them in frame - path consistency only.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Angle of the Pelvis Center displacement vector across the approach - it should track a consistent line toward the target rather than drifting. NOTE: the defender is NOT in frame in a solo clip, so alignment to THEIR position cannot be measured; only the consistency and straightness of the receiver's own approach path is assessable.

records.name: WR - First Steps - Blocking - Pad Level at Contact
records.ideal_execution_standard: At engagement the shoulders stay low - at or below the defender's pad level - with the torso angled forward so the receiver wins the leverage battle rather than being stood up.
records.fault_trigger: Engaging with pads high or the torso upright, letting the defender get underneath and upright the receiver, who then loses the block immediately. (Relative pad level needs the defender in frame.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Angle of the Spine vector (Pelvis Center to Sternum) relative to vertical at the engagement frame, plus absolute shoulder-midpoint height in torso lengths. NOTE: whether the receiver's pads are BELOW THE DEFENDER'S needs the defender in frame - in a solo clip only the receiver's own pad height and torso angle are assessable.

records.name: WR - First Steps - Blocking - Post-Contact Cleat Drive
records.ideal_execution_standard: The feet keep driving after contact, moving the defender while the base stays wide and the knees stay bent - the block is sustained rather than a single hit.
records.fault_trigger: Stopping the feet on contact and leaning on the defender, or standing up and narrowing the base after the hit - either way the block is lost within a second.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Forward velocity of Pelvis Center sustained after the contact frame, together with base width and knee flexion held at their engagement values. The measurement is all three continuing together - drive without losing the base or standing up.

records.name: WR - First Steps - Blocking - Short Choppy Step Cadence
records.ideal_execution_standard: The final two steps before contact shorten and quicken, keeping the feet under the body so the receiver can react instantly if the defender moves laterally.
records.fault_trigger: Arriving on long strides rather than chopping the feet down, leaving the receiver committed and unable to adjust when the defender moves.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Step frequency across the final two steps before contact, plus the ratio of ground contact time to flight time. Short choppy steps show as high frequency and a high contact-time ratio - the feet stay near the ground rather than striding out.

records.name: WR - First Steps - Blocking - Wide Base Preservation
records.ideal_execution_standard: The base stays wide throughout the approach - noticeably wider than a running stride - so the receiver keeps blocking leverage and can react laterally to the defender.
records.fault_trigger: Base narrowing into a normal running stride as the receiver closes, so he arrives with no lateral leverage and gets moved off the block on contact.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Lateral distance between the ankles at each ground contact through the approach, expressed in shoulder widths (L-R Shoulder as the scale unit) - should remain at or above 1.0x, significantly wider than a normal running stride. NOTE: the 1.0x figure is an uncalibrated starting reference.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Diamond Release - The Attack Step - Footwork
records.ideal_execution_standard: The back foot fires outward on a sharp 45 degree diagonal toward the inside lane, launching straight onto the diagonal track with no ground given up first.
records.fault_trigger: SOFT FIRST STEP - taking a tentative, short step instead of an aggressive 45 degree launch. The receiver must look like he is sprinting a slant from step one. Also: losing ground backward before the step fires.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Angle of the rear ankle's displacement relative to the stance facing - target is a sharp 45 degree diagonal toward the inside lane. Plus displacement magnitude, and confirmation of no backward ground loss along the release heading before the step fires. NOTE: resolved in the image plane against the heading, not via MediaPipe Z. The 45 degree figure is an uncalibrated starting reference.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Diamond Release - The Attack Step - Hands
records.ideal_execution_standard: The arms pump hard at chest height in a genuine sprint-start rhythm, matching what a real slant release would look like.
records.fault_trigger: Passive or low-amplitude arm action that does not match a real sprint, leaving the upper body out of step with the feet and weakening the fake.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Amplitude and frequency of wrist displacement front-to-back at lower-Sternum height, plus contralateral timing against the legs. The pattern should match a genuine sprint start, not a token arm movement.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Diamond Release - The Attack Step - Head / Eyes
records.ideal_execution_standard: The head locks straight down the 45 degree inside path from the first step, selling the route rather than checking on the defender.
records.fault_trigger: LOOKING AT THE DEFENDER - peeking at the DB instead of locking down the 45 degree track, which breaks the illusion before it is established. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) aligning with the 45 degree inside path, held there rather than turning toward the defender. NOTE: orientation only - actual EYE GAZE is not measurable from the 33-point pose model, and the defender is not in frame in a solo clip.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Diamond Release - The Attack Step - Hips
records.ideal_execution_standard: The hips accelerate along the 45 degree path and rotate fully onto the inside diagonal, committing the whole body to the fake from the first step.
records.fault_trigger: Hips staying square while only the feet take the diagonal, so the fake is not sold and a disciplined defender reads the outside release immediately.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Acceleration of Pelvis Center along the 45 degree diagonal, resolved in the image plane, plus the angle of the hip line (L-R Hip vector) which should rotate fully to align with that diagonal heading. Both should commit together on the first step.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Diamond Release - The Attack Step - Knees
records.ideal_execution_standard: The drive leg holds an acute bend - roughly 110 to 130 degrees - producing maximum ground force to launch onto the diagonal.
records.fault_trigger: Drive leg too straight at push-off, producing little ground force, so the attack step lacks the urgency needed to make the fake believable.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Knee flexion angle of the lead/drive leg from the Hip-Knee-Ankle vector at push-off. Reference range 110-130 degrees - acute enough to maximise ground force production out of the stance. NOTE: this range is an uncalibrated starting reference, not a rule.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Diamond Release - The Attack Step - Shoulders
records.ideal_execution_standard: The shoulders rotate fully square to the 45 degree line with the torso driving low and forward, exactly as they would on a genuine slant.
records.fault_trigger: Shoulders lagging behind the feet or staying upright rather than driving low onto the diagonal, so the upper body never commits to the lie.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Shoulder-line angle (L-R Shoulder vector) rotating to square with the 45 degree diagonal, plus torso drive angle of the Pelvis-Center-to-Sternum vector relative to vertical, which should stay low and forward. NOTE: resolved as image-plane angles, not via MediaPipe Z.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Diamond Release - The Breakout - Footwork
records.ideal_execution_standard: The plant foot drives explosively back toward the outside, the step reversing direction sharply enough to complete the diamond path and escape into the open lane.
records.fault_trigger: A rounded or gradual change of direction rather than a sharp reversal, so the diamond flattens into a curve and the defender recovers the ground the fake bought.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Angle of the first step out of the plant relative to the incoming 45 degree diagonal - a sharp direction reversal forming the diamond path. Plus peak acceleration of Pelvis Center along the new outside heading, and the contact time of the push-off. Resolved in the image plane, not via MediaPipe Z.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Diamond Release - The Breakout - Hands
records.ideal_execution_standard: The trailing arm executes a heavy downward chop past the shoulder line, clearing the defender's arms as the receiver breaks back to the outside.
records.fault_trigger: No hand action at the breakout, or an arm path that never crosses the shoulder line, leaving a recovering defender's hands attached through the escape. (Specific hand technique needs the Hand landmarker.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak downward and inward velocity of the trailing wrist and elbow, and whether that path crosses the shoulder line, timed against the breakout push-off. NOTE: the specific hand technique (swipe vs chop) needs the Hand landmarker; the arm path and velocity are measurable from pose.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Diamond Release - The Breakout - Head / Eyes
records.ideal_execution_standard: The head snaps round toward the sideline and upfield the instant the breakout fires, re-establishing vision to locate the quarterback and track the football.
records.fault_trigger: Head coming round slowly after the breakout, so the receiver is late finding the quarterback and the ball on a route designed to come out quickly. (Gaze and ball location are not pose-measurable.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak angular velocity of head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) snapping from the inside fake toward the sideline and upfield, plus the time taken to complete the rotation. NOTE: orientation only - actual EYE GAZE is not measurable from the 33-point pose model, and locating the quarterback or the football needs ball tracking.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Diamond Release - The Breakout - Hips
records.ideal_execution_standard: The hips snap violently open toward the sideline, flipping the body off the inside track and onto the outside release in one decisive rotation.
records.fault_trigger: Hips opening slowly or only partway, so the receiver drifts out of the cut rather than exploding, and the separation the fake created is given straight back.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak angular velocity of the hip line (L-R Hip vector) rotating from the inside diagonal to open toward the sideline, plus the total angular change and the time taken to complete it. The rotation should fire at the plant, not trail it.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Diamond Release - The Breakout - Knees
records.ideal_execution_standard: The outside knee drives high toward the sideline and upfield, taking immediate ground and building instant separation out of the cut.
records.fault_trigger: Low knee drive out of the breakout, so the first strides are short and the receiver takes too long to convert the cut into separation.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak vertical height of the outside knee relative to Pelvis Center (knee drive), expressed in torso lengths, plus the direction of that knee's travel toward the sideline and upfield.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Diamond Release - The Breakout - Shoulders
records.ideal_execution_standard: The inside shoulder rolls away from the defender as the receiver breaks out, turning the chest off them and eliminating the jersey surface they could grab.
records.fault_trigger: LEAVING THE CHEST EXPOSED - turning back outside with the chest wide open, which invites a trailing defender to land a heavy recovery punch and push the receiver off his path.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Rotation of the shoulder line (L-R Shoulder vector) so the inside shoulder turns away from the defender, reducing the frontal width of the torso. Measured as the image-plane shoulder-line angle relative to the new outside heading. NOTE: resolved in the image plane, not via MediaPipe Z.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Diamond Release - The Diamond Cut - Footwork
records.ideal_execution_standard: On the third step the outside foot slams into the turf along the 45 degree line and grips, acting as a violent brake that kills the inside momentum in one contact.
records.fault_trigger: The plant foot sliding or drifting at contact rather than gripping, so the momentum is not arrested and the receiver needs extra steps to change direction.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Horizontal ankle velocity of the outside (plant) foot at ground contact - target is zero drift, the foot gripping rather than sliding. Plus the rate at which Pelvis Center velocity along the 45 degree diagonal falls to zero, which measures how completely the forward momentum was arrested. Contact time from strike to toe-off indicates the violence of the brake.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Diamond Release - The Diamond Cut - Hands
records.ideal_execution_standard: The outside hand crosses over the chest frame at the plant, shielding the body against any late contact from a defender closing on the fake.
records.fault_trigger: Hands staying wide or low at the plant, leaving the chest unprotected at the exact moment a defender who bought the fake is arriving. (Finger and grip detail needs the Hand landmarker.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Horizontal position of the outside wrist relative to Sternum at the plant - it should cross the body's midline to shield the chest. Plus elbow flexion angle confirming a tucked protective position rather than an extended arm.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Diamond Release - The Diamond Cut - Head / Eyes
records.ideal_execution_standard: The head holds the inside fake alignment right up to the exact plant frame, then prepares to snap back - the deception is maintained to the last possible instant.
records.fault_trigger: Head starting to turn back outside before the plant lands, giving the defender an early warning and letting them jump the breakout. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) held on the inside fake alignment right up to the plant frame, with rotation beginning only at or after that frame. The measurement is the TIMING of the turn relative to the plant's ground contact. NOTE: orientation only - actual EYE GAZE is not measurable from the 33-point pose model.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Diamond Release - The Diamond Cut - Hips
records.ideal_execution_standard: The hips drop sharply and shift slightly back at the plant, sinking to absorb the forward momentum and load the push back outside.
records.fault_trigger: POP-UP BRAKING - letting the chest and hips rise when trying to stop. Without sinking the hips to absorb the momentum, the receiver slides or stumbles instead of cutting cleanly.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Abrupt vertical drop of Pelvis Center at the plant, expressed in torso lengths, plus a slight rearward shift resolved in the image plane against the diagonal heading. Both indicate the hips sinking to absorb momentum. NOTE: resolved in the image plane, not via MediaPipe Z.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Diamond Release - The Diamond Cut - Knees
records.ideal_execution_standard: The planting knee flexes deep - roughly 90 to 110 degrees - creating a spring-loaded platform to drive back out toward the sideline.
records.fault_trigger: Planting on a stiff, straight leg, which cannot absorb the momentum or store energy - the receiver slides through the cut and the breakout has no power.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Knee flexion angle of the planting leg from the Hip-Knee-Ankle vector at ground contact. Reference range 90-110 degrees - deep enough to create a spring-loaded push platform. NOTE: this range is an uncalibrated starting reference, not a rule.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Diamond Release - The Diamond Cut - Shoulders
records.ideal_execution_standard: The shoulders stay over the toes as the plant foot lands, keeping the body stacked over the brake and ready to snap back toward the outside.
records.fault_trigger: Chest rising or the shoulders falling behind the plant foot, so the weight sits back and the receiver cannot push cleanly back to the outside.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Horizontal position of the shoulder midpoint relative to the plant foot's Foot Index at ground contact - the shoulders should stay over the toes rather than behind them. Chest rise at the plant is the fault signal, measured as upward displacement of Sternum.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Diamond Release - The Push Step - Footwork
records.ideal_execution_standard: The opposite foot drives down the exact same 45 degree line as the first step, taking real ground inside so the fake reads as a committed route.
records.fault_trigger: The second step drifting off the 45 degree line or shortening, so the diagonal track bends and the defender reads that the inside move is not real.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Angle of the second step's ankle displacement relative to the first - both should lie along the same 45 degree line. Deviation between the two step angles is the measurement. Plus displacement magnitude, confirming real ground gained rather than a token second step.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Diamond Release - The Push Step - Hands
records.ideal_execution_standard: The arm pump continues at full amplitude through the push step, sustaining the impression of a slant or post being run at full effort.
records.fault_trigger: Arm pump dropping off during the push step, which signals to the defender that the receiver is about to stop rather than continuing inside.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Amplitude and frequency of wrist displacement across the push step, sustained at the level established on the attack step. A drop in amplitude indicates the receiver is easing off before the cut.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Diamond Release - The Push Step - Head / Eyes
records.ideal_execution_standard: The head stays locked straight down the inside path through the push step, holding the deception right up until the plant.
records.fault_trigger: Head turning back toward the outside before the plant, breaking the deception early and letting the defender sit on the breakout. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) held locked on the 45 degree inside path across the push step, measured as low angular variance. Any rotation toward the outside before the plant is a tell. NOTE: orientation only - actual EYE GAZE is not measurable from the 33-point pose model.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Diamond Release - The Push Step - Hips
records.ideal_execution_standard: The hips stay dropped and fully committed to the inside trajectory, holding the low sprinting position that makes the fake believable.
records.fault_trigger: Hips rising through the push step, so the receiver looks like he is preparing to stop rather than sprinting a route - the defender reads the cut coming.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Vertical height of Pelvis Center held low across the push step, expressed in torso lengths, plus continued acceleration along the 45 degree diagonal. The hips should stay dropped and committed rather than rising as speed builds.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Diamond Release - The Push Step - Knees
records.ideal_execution_standard: The back knee drives high and hard on the push step, simulating full sprint acceleration so nothing about the movement suggests a fake.
records.fault_trigger: Low knee drive on the push step, betraying that the receiver is not truly accelerating and is already preparing to plant.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak vertical height of the back knee relative to Pelvis Center (knee drive), expressed in torso lengths, on the push step. The lift should match a genuine vertical sprint stride rather than a shortened fake stride.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Diamond Release - The Push Step - Shoulders
records.ideal_execution_standard: The torso stays low and forward in an aggressive sprinting posture through the push step, matching what a genuine slant would look like.
records.fault_trigger: Torso rising toward upright during the push step, which tips that a plant is coming rather than a continued sprint inside.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Torso drive angle of the Pelvis-Center-to-Sternum vector relative to vertical, held low and forward across the push step. Cross-check against the hip-to-knee vector to confirm a whole-body sprint posture rather than folding at the waist.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Kickstep Crossover - Crossover - Footwork
records.ideal_execution_standard: The push off the plant foot drives the rear foot sharply across the body's midline into the inside lane, committing hard enough to sell the inside release.
records.fault_trigger: A lazy crossover that never clears the midline, or one too slow to be believed - the defender does not bite and the outside lane never opens.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Lateral displacement of the rear ankle across the body's midline (defined by Pelvis Center) into the inside lane, resolved in the image plane, plus the peak lateral velocity of that crossover. Sharpness is the velocity; commitment is the displacement past the midline.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Kickstep Crossover - Crossover - Hands
records.ideal_execution_standard: The arms pump hard toward the inside lane in time with the crossover step, mimicking a genuine release so the fake is complete from feet to hands.
records.fault_trigger: Arms staying passive during the crossover, or pumping late so the upper body lags the feet and the fake looks manufactured. (Finger and grip detail needs the Hand landmarker.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak lateral velocity of the wrists toward the inside lane, resolved in the image plane, timed against the crossover step. The arm pump should fire with the foot and hips, not after them.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Kickstep Crossover - Crossover - Head / Eyes
records.ideal_execution_standard: The head snaps sharply toward the inside lane in time with the crossover, adding the final piece of the fake - the defender reads the eyes as well as the feet.
records.fault_trigger: Head staying still or turning too slowly during the crossover, leaving the fake incomplete. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak angular velocity of head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) toward the inside lane, timed against the crossover step. The measurement is the SPEED of the head snap, not just its end position. NOTE: orientation only - actual EYE GAZE is not measurable from the 33-point pose model.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Kickstep Crossover - Crossover - Hips
records.ideal_execution_standard: The hips drive hard laterally across the defender's face, rotating toward the inside lane so the whole body sells the fake rather than just the feet.
records.fault_trigger: Hips staying square while only the feet cross over - the fake is not sold, and the defender reads the outside release immediately.
