records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak lateral acceleration of Pelvis Center toward the inside lane, resolved in the image plane, plus rotation of the hip line (L-R Hip vector) toward that lane. Both should spike together to sell the inside move.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Kickstep Crossover - Crossover - Knees
records.ideal_execution_standard: The lead knee flexes and drives aggressively inward across the body, pointing along the inside fake path to sell the release direction.
records.fault_trigger: Lead knee staying square or trailing the foot across, so the lower body does not commit and the fake reads as a feint rather than a release.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Lead knee flexion angle plus the lateral direction of the knee's travel, measured from the Hip-Knee-Ankle vectors. The knee should drive inward across the body, pointing along the inside fake path rather than staying square or collapsing.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Kickstep Crossover - Crossover - Shoulders
records.ideal_execution_standard: The inside shoulder dips hard and the torso leans into the inside lane, committing the upper body to the fake so the defender has to honour it.
records.fault_trigger: Shoulders staying level through the crossover, so the upper body never sells the inside move and the defender stays square to the outside release.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Vertical drop of the inside shoulder relative to the outside shoulder (shoulder-line tilt angle), plus torso lean of the Pelvis-Center-to-Sternum vector toward the inside lane. A pronounced dip is the sell.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Kickstep Crossover - Kickstep - Footwork
records.ideal_execution_standard: The rear foot kicks directly behind the front foot to load the release, without giving up ground backward. The step loads the body rather than retreating from the line.
records.fault_trigger: Stepping backward and losing ground to the defender, or kicking the rear foot wide of the front foot rather than directly behind it, which widens the base and slows the escape.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Displacement of the rear ankle relative to the front foot, resolved in the image plane against the release heading. The rear ankle should travel directly behind the front foot with NO negative displacement along the heading (no ground lost backward). NOTE: resolved in the image plane, not via MediaPipe Z, which is unreliable monocular.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Kickstep Crossover - Kickstep - Hands
records.ideal_execution_standard: Hands stay active and up around lower chest height, ready to fight the defender's hands, never dropping below the hips.
records.fault_trigger: Hands dropping below the hips during the kickstep, leaving the receiver unable to counter the jam. (Finger and grip detail needs the Hand landmarker.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Vertical height of both wrists relative to Sternum and Pelvis Center - wrists should stay at or above lower-Sternum level and never drop below the hip line. Elbow angle for active vs collapsed arms.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Kickstep Crossover - Kickstep - Head / Eyes
records.ideal_execution_standard: The head stays level and locked forward toward the defender's belt line - reading the hips rather than the hands or the feet.
records.fault_trigger: Head dipping toward the feet or lifting off the defender's midsection line during the kickstep. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable, and the defender is not in frame - orientation only.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Head pitch and yaw from Nose position relative to the ear midpoint - the head should stay level, aimed forward at roughly defender belt/midsection height rather than dipping to the feet or lifting. NOTE: orientation only - actual EYE GAZE is not measurable from the 33-point pose model, and the defender is not in frame in a solo clip, so the target line cannot be confirmed.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Kickstep Crossover - Kickstep - Hips
records.ideal_execution_standard: Hips stay sunk low through the kickstep, holding the loaded height established in the stance with no upward rise.
records.fault_trigger: Hips rising during the kickstep, unloading the legs and costing the elastic energy needed to escape.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Vertical height of Pelvis Center across the kickstep, expressed in torso lengths. Target is zero net upward displacement - the hips stay sunk at the height established in the stance.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Kickstep Crossover - Kickstep - Knees
records.ideal_execution_standard: The front knee holds an acute bend - roughly 100 to 120 degrees - absorbing force and storing elastic energy for the escape rather than straightening under the load.
records.fault_trigger: Front knee straightening or losing its bend during the kickstep, so no energy is stored and the escape has to be generated from a standing start.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Front knee flexion angle from the Hip-Knee-Ankle vectors. Reference range 100-120 degrees - acute enough to absorb force and store elastic energy. NOTE: this range is an uncalibrated starting reference, not a rule. Which leg is 'front' is resolved from the stance stagger.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Kickstep Crossover - Kickstep - Shoulders
records.ideal_execution_standard: The torso holds a slight forward lean over the toes while the shoulders stay square to the defender, giving away nothing about the intended release direction.
records.fault_trigger: Shoulders rotating open during the kickstep and telegraphing the release, or the torso leaning back away from the defender instead of staying over the toes.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Torso tilt angle (Pelvis Center to Sternum) relative to vertical - a slight forward lean over the toes. Plus shoulder-line angle relative to the release heading, which should stay square (near zero rotation). NOTE: shoulder squareness resolved as the image-plane angle of the L-R Shoulder vector, not via MediaPipe Z.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Kickstep Crossover - Outside Burst - Footwork
records.ideal_execution_standard: The crossover foot plants and immediately pushes off into the outside lane - no gather step, no pause. The redirect is instantaneous, converting the fake straight into the escape.
records.fault_trigger: A gather step or hesitation between the crossover and the burst, giving the defender time to recover and closing the outside lane the fake just opened.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Time between crossover foot ground contact and toe-off (contact time - shorter is better), plus peak acceleration of Pelvis Center toward the outside vertical lane immediately after, resolved in the image plane. The measurement is the instantaneous redirect, not the top speed.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Kickstep Crossover - Outside Burst - Hands
records.ideal_execution_standard: The trailing arm drives sharply past the shoulder plane - swipe, chop or swim - clearing the defender's hands as the body escapes outside.
records.fault_trigger: No hand action at the escape, or an arm path that never clears the shoulder plane, leaving the defender's hands attached through the release. (Specific hand technique needs the Hand landmarker.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak vertical velocity of the trailing wrist and whether it passes above the shoulder plane (swipe/chop/swim), timed against the burst push-off. The measurement is the velocity and the clearance height, not the hand shape. NOTE: the specific hand action (swipe vs chop vs swim) needs the Hand landmarker; the arm path is measurable from pose.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Kickstep Crossover - Outside Burst - Head / Eyes
records.ideal_execution_standard: The head snaps back upfield to align with the route, re-establishing vision quickly so the receiver can track the cushion and find the ball.
records.fault_trigger: Head staying turned toward the fake after the escape, or turning back slowly, so the receiver loses track of the defender and is late finding the ball. (Gaze and ball location are not pose-measurable.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) rotating back from the inside fake to align with the outside route heading, plus the time taken to complete that rotation. NOTE: orientation only - actual EYE GAZE is not measurable from the 33-point pose model, and locating the ball needs ball tracking.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Kickstep Crossover - Outside Burst - Hips
records.ideal_execution_standard: The hips rotate sharply from the inside fake toward the sideline and upfield, converting the lateral momentum of the crossover into vertical drive up the field.
records.fault_trigger: Hips rotating slowly or incompletely, so the receiver drifts sideways out of the release instead of driving upfield, losing ground on the route stem.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Angular velocity of the hip line (L-R Hip vector) rotating from the inside fake toward the outside vertical lane, plus the change in Pelvis Center trajectory heading from lateral to upfield. Both measure the conversion of lateral momentum into vertical drive.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Kickstep Crossover - Outside Burst - Knees
records.ideal_execution_standard: The outside knee drives high and the trailing leg extends fully at push-off, taking ground upfield immediately rather than shuffling out of the release.
records.fault_trigger: Low knee drive and an incomplete trailing-leg extension, so the first strides out of the release are short and the receiver takes too long to reach full speed.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak vertical height of the outside knee relative to Pelvis Center (knee drive), expressed in torso lengths, plus extension angle of the trailing leg from the Hip-Knee-Ankle vectors at push-off.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Kickstep Crossover - Outside Burst - Shoulders
records.ideal_execution_standard: The inside shoulder rolls away from the defender - getting skinny - so the receiver presents the narrowest possible surface as he clears the contact window.
records.fault_trigger: Running through the release square-shouldered, presenting a full chest for the defender to get hands on and re-route the receiver.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Rotation of the shoulder line (L-R Shoulder vector) so the inside shoulder turns away from the defender's side, reducing the frontal width of the torso. Measured as the image-plane shoulder-line angle relative to the release heading - a larger rotation means a narrower profile presented. NOTE: resolved in the image plane, not via MediaPipe Z.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Kickstep Crossover - Plant Step - Footwork
records.ideal_execution_standard: The front foot plants firmly with no braking, and the feet stay tight within the body's frame - at or inside shoulder width - so the escape can fire in either direction.
records.fault_trigger: Planting with a braking action that kills momentum, or a base widening beyond shoulder width so the receiver has to gather before escaping.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Horizontal ankle velocity at the plant foot's ground contact - target is zero braking velocity along the release heading. Plus lateral distance between the ankles at the plant, which should stay at or below 1.0x shoulder width (L-R Shoulder as the scale unit).

records.name: WR - Press Release - Kickstep Crossover - Plant Step - Hands
records.ideal_execution_standard: The hands retract tight to the lower chest and ribcage in a compact ready position, loaded to swipe or punch as the escape begins.
records.fault_trigger: Hands hanging away from the frame or extended early, giving the defender something to grab and leaving nothing loaded for the escape. (Finger and grip detail needs the Hand landmarker.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Distance from each wrist to Sternum, expressed in torso lengths - the wrists should retract close to the lower Sternum/ribcage into a compact ready position. Plus elbow flexion angle for a tucked vs extended arm.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Kickstep Crossover - Plant Step - Head / Eyes
records.ideal_execution_standard: The head stays level through the plant, holding a neutral forward line rather than dropping to look at the feet as the body loads.
records.fault_trigger: Head dipping toward the feet as the body loads at the plant, losing sight of the defender at the moment the release is about to start. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Head pitch from Nose position relative to the ear midpoint - should hold a neutral, level horizontal orientation with no downward dip toward the feet at the plant. NOTE: orientation only - actual EYE GAZE is not measurable from the 33-point pose model.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Kickstep Crossover - Plant Step - Hips
records.ideal_execution_standard: The hips drop and shift slightly back over the plant foot, compressing like a spring so the escape can launch in any direction.
records.fault_trigger: Hips staying high or drifting forward past the plant foot, so the spring never loads and the escape has no power behind it.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Vertical drop of Pelvis Center at the plant, expressed in torso lengths, plus a slight rearward shift resolved in the image plane against the release heading. Both indicate the hips loading like a compressed spring. NOTE: resolved in the image plane, not via MediaPipe Z.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Kickstep Crossover - Plant Step - Knees
records.ideal_execution_standard: Both knees bend deeper at the plant, dropping the receiver into a loaded crouch that can launch in any direction.
records.fault_trigger: Knees staying at their kickstep angle or straightening at the plant, so the receiver is upright and committed rather than loaded and able to go either way.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Bilateral knee flexion angles from the Hip-Knee-Ankle vectors on both legs, compared against their kickstep values - both should REDUCE into a deeper loaded crouch at the plant. The measurement is the reduction, not an absolute angle.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Kickstep Crossover - Plant Step - Shoulders
records.ideal_execution_standard: The shoulders stay tucked inside the width of the knees, keeping the frame compact so the defender cannot read which way the release is going.
records.fault_trigger: A shoulder drifting outside the knee line at the plant, widening the frame and telegraphing the release direction before the crossover begins.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Lateral position of each shoulder relative to the lateral boundary of the knees - the shoulders should stay inside that boundary (tucked within the frame). Measured as horizontal offsets in the image plane.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The Hesitation - Footwork
records.ideal_execution_standard: The sliding foot plants firmly and the lateral movement stops dead for a fraction of a second, holding the wide base while the defender is frozen.
records.fault_trigger: Drifting through the hesitation rather than stopping cleanly, so there is no freeze for the defender to react to and the bait never lands.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Lateral velocity of the sliding ankle at the end of the slide - target is a momentary drop to zero, a clean freeze rather than a gradual decay. Plus confirmation the wide base established in the slide is held during the freeze frames.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The Hesitation - Hands
records.ideal_execution_standard: The hands retract tight to the lower ribcage into a compact ready position, loaded to strike as soon as contact comes.
records.fault_trigger: Hands hanging loose or away from the frame during the pause, giving the defender something to grab and leaving nothing loaded for the strike. (Finger and grip detail needs the Hand landmarker.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Distance from each wrist to Sternum, expressed in torso lengths - the wrists should retract close to the lower ribcage into a compact ready position. Plus elbow flexion angle for a tucked rather than extended arm.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The Hesitation - Head / Eyes
records.ideal_execution_standard: The head stays locked forward on the defender through the pause, reading whether their hips open or freeze before the receiver commits to the vertical.
records.fault_trigger: Head turning upfield during the hesitation, tipping the vertical release before the read is complete. (Gaze and the defender's reaction are not pose-measurable.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Head yaw and pitch from Nose position relative to the ear midpoint, held stable and forward across the hesitation frames. NOTE: orientation only - actual EYE GAZE is not measurable from the 33-point pose model, and the defender is not in frame in a solo clip, so whether the receiver actually READ the defender's hips cannot be confirmed - only that the head was oriented to do so.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The Hesitation - Hips
records.ideal_execution_standard: The hips stay low and loaded through the hesitation, holding the compressed position so the forward transition can fire without a reset.
records.fault_trigger: Hips rising during the pause, unloading the spring - the receiver then has to sink again before transitioning, which gives the defender time to recover.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Vertical height of Pelvis Center across the hesitation frames, expressed in torso lengths - it should hold low with no upward drift, preserving the compressed-spring position.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The Hesitation - Knees
records.ideal_execution_standard: Both knees stay deep and stable through the pause, absorbing the lateral momentum and holding balance on the wide base.
records.fault_trigger: Knees straightening or wobbling during the hesitation, so the receiver loses balance on the wide base or unloads the legs before the transition.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Bilateral knee flexion angles held across the hesitation frames, compared against their values at the end of the slide - the angles should be maintained and stable, absorbing the lateral force without collapsing or extending.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The Hesitation - Shoulders
records.ideal_execution_standard: The torso tilts slightly forward over the toes to threaten an immediate vertical launch from the side lane, while the shoulders stay quiet and give nothing away.
records.fault_trigger: LEANING EARLY - tilting the head or shoulders toward the intended vertical route during the micro-pause, which completely tips off the true direction. Also: leaning back rather than forward, so no vertical threat is presented.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Torso lean of the Pelvis-Center-to-Sternum vector relative to vertical - a slight forward tilt over the toes, threatening a vertical launch. Plus angular variance of the shoulder line across the hesitation frames, which should stay low (quiet shoulders, no early lean toward the eventual release).

records.name: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The Lateral Slide - Footwork
records.ideal_execution_standard: The receiver pushes off the front foot and slides the back foot sideways, feet staying wide and parallel and low to the ground, moving laterally to bypass the jam rather than through it.
records.fault_trigger: THE BUNNY HOP - jumping or leaping sideways instead of sliding. Hopping lifts both feet too high off the ground, leaving the receiver completely vulnerable if a defender jams him mid-air. Also: feet crossing rather than staying parallel.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Lateral displacement of the rear ankle away from the front foot, resolved in the image plane perpendicular to the release heading. Base width expands to at least 1.2x shoulder width (L-R Shoulder as the scale unit), with feet remaining parallel and zero ankle crossing. Cross-check vertical ankle displacement - a slide keeps the feet low, a hop spikes them upward. NOTE: the 1.2x figure is an uncalibrated starting reference.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The Lateral Slide - Hands
records.ideal_execution_standard: The hands stay up at lower chest height and relaxed through the slide, ready to react the instant a jam comes.
records.fault_trigger: Hands dropping as the receiver concentrates on the footwork, leaving him with no answer if the defender reaches out mid-slide. (Finger and grip detail needs the Hand landmarker.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Vertical height of both wrists relative to Sternum, held across the slide at lower-Sternum level. Plus elbow flexion angle for relaxed-but-ready rather than rigid or collapsed arms.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The Lateral Slide - Head / Eyes
records.ideal_execution_standard: The head stays level and locked on the defender's belt line throughout the slide, tracking them laterally without dropping to the feet.
records.fault_trigger: Head dropping to watch the feet during the slide, or turning upfield early and telegraphing the vertical release. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Head yaw and pitch from Nose position relative to the ear midpoint, held level and locked forward across the slide. NOTE: orientation only - actual EYE GAZE is not measurable from the 33-point pose model, and the defender is not in frame in a solo clip, so the target line cannot be confirmed.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The Lateral Slide - Hips
records.ideal_execution_standard: The hips travel horizontally at a constant height with no rotation, staying square to the defender so the slide gives away nothing about the eventual release.
records.fault_trigger: Hips rotating during the slide, opening the receiver to the defender and tipping the release; or the hips rising and falling, which turns a glide into a hop.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Horizontal track of Pelvis Center across the slide, plus the angle of the hip line (L-R Hip vector) which should hold zero rotation, and vertical height of Pelvis Center which should stay constant. The measurement is a flat, level, non-rotating traverse.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The Lateral Slide - Knees
records.ideal_execution_standard: Both knees hold a consistent bend - roughly 120 to 140 degrees - through the slide, producing a smooth lateral glide with no upward bounce.
records.fault_trigger: Knees extending during the slide, which pops the body upward into a hop; or collapsing so deep the receiver cannot cover ground laterally.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Bilateral knee flexion angles from the Hip-Knee-Ankle vectors, held across the slide. Reference range 120-140 degrees. Cross-check vertical variance of Pelvis Center - upward spikes indicate hopping rather than gliding. NOTE: the 120-140 range is an uncalibrated starting reference, not a rule.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The Lateral Slide - Shoulders
records.ideal_execution_standard: The shoulders stay wide, level and square to the defender, moving with the hips rather than rotating independently of them.
records.fault_trigger: Shoulders rotating away from the hips during the slide, disconnecting the upper body and signalling the release direction before the receiver has committed.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Angle between the shoulder line and the hip line (rotational separation) - target is zero. Plus shoulder-line angle relative to the release heading, which should stay square, and shoulder-line tilt, which should stay level. NOTE: squareness resolved as the image-plane shoulder-line angle, not via MediaPipe Z.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The React and Plant - Footwork
records.ideal_execution_standard: The outside foot slams aggressively into the turf and grips, arresting all lateral momentum in one contact so it can be converted straight into forward drive.
records.fault_trigger: SOFT CLEAT PLANT - failing to slam the outside foot into the turf with force. A soft plant results in a slow, sluggish transition from horizontal to vertical, and the foot drifts rather than gripping.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Horizontal ankle velocity of the outside (plant) foot at ground contact - target is zero drift, the foot gripping rather than sliding. Plus the rate at which the lateral velocity of Pelvis Center falls to zero after the plant, which measures how completely the sideways momentum was arrested. Contact time from strike to toe-off indicates how cleanly the force was delivered.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The React and Plant - Hands
records.ideal_execution_standard: The hands come up fast into an aggressive strike position as the plant lands, ready to meet the defender if they reach out at the transition.
records.fault_trigger: Hands staying passive or low through the plant, leaving the receiver defenceless at the exact moment the defender is most likely to reach. (Specific hand technique needs the Hand landmarker.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak upward velocity of the wrists as the plant lands, and whether the hands reach a strike-ready height relative to Sternum. The hand action should fire with the plant, not after it. NOTE: the specific hand technique needs the Hand landmarker; arm path and timing are measurable from pose.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The React and Plant - Head / Eyes
records.ideal_execution_standard: The head begins turning upfield toward the release lane as the plant lands, leading the body into the vertical transition.
records.fault_trigger: Head turning well before the plant (telegraphing the vertical) or lagging behind it, so the body commits before the receiver has picked up the lane. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Onset and angular velocity of head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) rotating toward the upfield release lane, timed against the plant's ground contact. NOTE: orientation only - actual EYE GAZE is not measurable from the 33-point pose model.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The React and Plant - Hips
records.ideal_execution_standard: The hips sink further at the plant, loading the lower body so the lateral energy can be redirected into forward acceleration.
records.fault_trigger: Hips staying level or rising at the plant instead of sinking, so nothing loads and the transition to vertical has no power behind it.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Additional vertical drop of Pelvis Center at the plant, expressed in torso lengths, measured against its height during the hesitation. The drop should be a further sink, not a return to standing.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The React and Plant - Knees
records.ideal_execution_standard: The planting knee bends sharply - roughly 90 to 110 degrees - absorbing the lateral energy of the slide and converting it into straight-line power.
records.fault_trigger: Planting on a stiff, straight leg, which cannot absorb the lateral force - the receiver slides through the plant or has to take a recovery step before going vertical.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Knee flexion angle of the planting leg from the Hip-Knee-Ankle vector at ground contact. Reference range 90-110 degrees - acute enough to absorb the lateral kinetic energy and convert it into straight-line power. NOTE: this range is an uncalibrated starting reference, not a rule.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The React and Plant - Shoulders
records.ideal_execution_standard: The inside shoulder dips at the plant, lowering the chest profile and getting skinny against the defender's leverage as the transition begins.
records.fault_trigger: Staying square and upright through the plant, presenting a full chest just as the receiver commits and giving the defender a clean target to re-route.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Vertical drop of the inside shoulder relative to the outside shoulder (shoulder-line tilt angle) at the plant, plus the resulting reduction in the torso's frontal profile. A pronounced dip lowers the chest profile against the defender's leverage.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The Vertical Burst - Footwork
records.ideal_execution_standard: The plant foot drives explosively forward, accelerating the receiver past the defender's hip plane and clearing their level in one burst rather than easing into the route.
records.fault_trigger: A slow or gradual push-off out of the plant, so the receiver never clears the defender's level and stays inside their reach as the route develops. (Defender position is not in frame - path and acceleration only.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak forward acceleration of Pelvis Center along the release heading immediately after the plant's toe-off, resolved in the image plane, plus the contact time of that push-off. NOTE: resolved in the image plane against the heading, not via MediaPipe Z. The defender's hip plane is not in frame in a solo clip, so clearance is inferred from the path rather than confirmed.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The Vertical Burst - Hands
records.ideal_execution_standard: The trailing arm drives violently past the shoulder plane - swipe, chop or club-rip - shattering the defender's reach as the receiver clears vertically.
records.fault_trigger: DROPPING THE HANDS - letting the arms trail behind the body, leaving no protection against a recovering defender's arm bar or jersey pull. Also: an arm path that never clears the shoulder plane. (Specific hand technique needs the Hand landmarker.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak velocity of the trailing wrist and elbow, and whether that path passes above the shoulder plane (swipe / chop / club-rip), timed against the burst stride. NOTE: the specific hand technique needs the Hand landmarker; the arm path, height and velocity are measurable from pose.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The Vertical Burst - Head / Eyes
records.ideal_execution_standard: The head comes fully round to track upfield along the route, re-establishing vision quickly so the receiver can process cushion and locate the ball.
records.fault_trigger: Head still turned toward the slide side after the burst, or coming round slowly, so the receiver is late reading coverage and late finding the ball. (Gaze and ball location are not pose-measurable.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) completing its rotation to align with the upfield route trajectory, plus the time taken from the plant to reach that alignment. NOTE: orientation only - actual EYE GAZE is not measurable from the 33-point pose model, and locating the football needs ball tracking.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The Vertical Burst - Hips
records.ideal_execution_standard: The hips flip sharply from the lateral slide orientation to point straight upfield, locking the receiver onto the vertical track in a single decisive rotation.
records.fault_trigger: Hips rotating slowly or only partway, leaving the receiver running at an angle across the field rather than vertically - the slide's advantage is lost in the transition.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Angular change of the hip line (L-R Hip vector) from its lateral orientation during the slide to alignment with the upfield heading - approximately a 90 degree flip. Plus the angular velocity of that rotation and the time taken to complete it.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The Vertical Burst - Knees
records.ideal_execution_standard: The lead knee drives high out of the transition, taking immediate ground upfield and accelerating the receiver toward top speed.
records.fault_trigger: Low knee drive out of the burst, so the first strides are short and shuffling and the receiver takes too long to reach full speed after the transition.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak vertical height of the lead knee relative to Pelvis Center (knee drive), expressed in torso lengths, across the first strides of the burst.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The Vertical Burst - Shoulders
records.ideal_execution_standard: The inside shoulder rolls away as the receiver bursts past, turning the chest off the defender and eliminating the jersey surface they could grab.
records.fault_trigger: Bursting through square-shouldered, leaving a full jersey surface exposed for a recovering defender to grab as the receiver passes.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Rotation of the shoulder line (L-R Shoulder vector) so the inside shoulder turns away from the defender's side, reducing the frontal width of the torso. Measured as the image-plane shoulder-line angle relative to the release heading. NOTE: resolved in the image plane, not via MediaPipe Z.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Split Release - The Hesitation - Footwork
records.ideal_execution_standard: The feet stay planted wide and parallel through the read - completely still, holding the base while the defender is frozen.
records.fault_trigger: Feet shuffling, creeping or resetting during the read, which breaks the freeze and tells the defender a move is coming.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Positional variance of both ankles across the read frames - target is zero displacement, the feet planted and still. Plus confirmation the ankle separation and parallel alignment established in the split are held.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Split Release - The Hesitation - Hands
records.ideal_execution_standard: The hands stay up at chest level and active through the read, ready to strike the moment the defender's hands come.
records.fault_trigger: Hands dropping or going passive during the hesitation, leaving the receiver with nothing ready when the jam arrives. (Finger and grip detail needs the Hand landmarker.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Vertical height of both wrists relative to Sternum held across the read frames - staying at chest level. Plus wrist positional variance as an activity measure: active hands show small continuous motion rather than being frozen or dropped.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Split Release - The Hesitation - Head / Eyes
records.ideal_execution_standard: The head stays locked on the defender's midsection through the read, processing whether they freeze, lean, or slide before the receiver commits.
records.fault_trigger: RUSHING THE READ - turning the head toward the intended path before the defender has declared, or skipping the read entirely and committing blind. (Gaze and the defender's reaction are not pose-measurable.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Head yaw and pitch from Nose position relative to the ear midpoint, held stable across the read frames on the defender's midsection line. NOTE: orientation only - actual EYE GAZE is not measurable from the 33-point pose model, and the defender is not in frame in a solo clip, so whether the receiver actually READ the leverage cannot be confirmed - only that the head was oriented to do so.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Split Release - The Hesitation - Hips
records.ideal_execution_standard: The hips stay low through the read, preserving the loaded position so the receiver can explode in whichever direction the defender opens.
records.fault_trigger: Hips rising during the hesitation, unloading the base - the receiver then has to re-sink before moving, which costs the advantage the split created.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Vertical height of Pelvis Center across the read frames, expressed in torso lengths - it should hold the low position established at the split with no upward drift.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Split Release - The Hesitation - Knees
records.ideal_execution_standard: Both knees hold their deep flexion through the read - loaded springs, ready to extend the instant the defender commits.
records.fault_trigger: Knees straightening during the hesitation, so the springs unload and the drive-off has to start from scratch.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Bilateral knee flexion angles held across the read frames, compared against their values at the split - the angles should be maintained, not increasing (standing up) or collapsing.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Split Release - The Hesitation - Shoulders
records.ideal_execution_standard: Quiet shoulders - no tilt, no rotation, no lean. The upper body gives away nothing while the receiver reads which way the defender is going.
records.fault_trigger: LEANING EARLY - tilting the head or shoulders toward the intended release during the micro-pause, which completely tips off the true direction and wastes the freeze.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Angular variance of the shoulder line (L-R Shoulder vector) across the read frames - target is zero early tilt or rotation. Quiet shoulders means low variance. Cross-check the shoulder-to-hip separation angle, which should also stay flat.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Split Release - The Plant & Drive - Footwork
records.ideal_execution_standard: The foot opposite the intended path slams cleanly into the turf with no slide, delivering full force to drive the body laterally and forward into the open lane.
records.fault_trigger: CLICK-BACK - dragging the driving foot instead of slamming it cleanly into the turf, which bleeds away the explosive power. Also: the foot sliding at contact rather than gripping.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Horizontal ankle velocity of the plant foot at ground contact - target is zero slide. Plus the plant foot's position relative to Pelvis Center: it plants on the OPPOSITE side to the intended release, so the push drives the body into the chosen lane. Contact time from strike to toe-off measures how cleanly the force was delivered.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Split Release - The Plant & Drive - Hands
records.ideal_execution_standard: The hands fire up and forward as the plant lands - striking, clearing or bypassing the defender's jam in the same instant the body drives.
records.fault_trigger: Hands staying passive through the drive, leaving the defender free to land a clean jam on a receiver who is already committed to a direction. (Specific hand technique needs the Hand landmarker.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak upward and forward acceleration of the wrists, timed against the plant foot's ground contact. The hand action should fire with the drive, not after it. NOTE: the specific hand technique (strike vs swipe vs bypass) needs the Hand landmarker; the arm path and timing are measurable from pose.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Split Release - The Plant & Drive - Head / Eyes
records.ideal_execution_standard: The head snaps toward the chosen attack path as the plant fires, committing the whole body to the direction in one motion.
records.fault_trigger: Head turning before the plant (telegraphing the direction) or well after it (leaving the receiver driving blind into the lane). (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak angular velocity of head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) rotating toward the chosen attack path, timed against the plant. NOTE: orientation only - actual EYE GAZE is not measurable from the 33-point pose model.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Split Release - The Plant & Drive - Hips
records.ideal_execution_standard: The hips turn and open violently toward the chosen lane the instant the plant foot hits, converting the loaded base into directional drive.
records.fault_trigger: Hips opening slowly or lagging behind the plant, so the drive has no rotational force behind it and the receiver pushes sideways instead of exploding through the lane.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak angular velocity of the hip line (L-R Hip vector) rotating toward the chosen release direction, timed against the plant foot's ground contact. The rotation should fire WITH the plant, not after it.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Split Release - The Plant & Drive - Knees
records.ideal_execution_standard: The drive leg extends fully to deliver every bit of force, while the lead knee flexes and drives forward to take immediate ground into the lane.
records.fault_trigger: Drive leg failing to extend fully, leaving force in the ground; or the lead knee not driving through, so the first stride out of the plant is short.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Drive-leg knee extension angle at push-off, approaching full extension (near 180 degrees), measured from the Hip-Knee-Ankle vector. Simultaneously the lead knee should FLEX to gain ground. The measurement is the opposing pair - full extension behind, flexion in front.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Split Release - The Plant & Drive - Shoulders
records.ideal_execution_standard: The leading shoulder dips into the direction of the release - getting skinny - so the receiver presents the smallest possible target as he attacks the lane.
records.fault_trigger: Driving into the lane square-shouldered and upright, presenting a full chest for the defender to get hands on and re-route the release.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Vertical drop of the leading shoulder relative to the trailing shoulder (shoulder-line tilt) toward the release direction, timed against the plant. A pronounced dip narrows the target area presented to the defender.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Split Release - The Split - Footwork
records.ideal_execution_standard: Both feet leave the ground at the same instant, the back foot snapping forward and the front foot back, landing parallel and wider than shoulder width to establish a balanced, uncommitted base.
records.fault_trigger: OVER-SPLITTING - landing far too wide, which locks up the hips so the receiver cannot push off to change direction. Also: feet leaving the ground at different times rather than together, or landing staggered instead of parallel.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Both ankles leaving the ground within the same frame window (simultaneous lift), then rear ankle displacing forward and front ankle slightly back along the release heading, landing parallel. Final ankle separation greater than 1.0x shoulder width (L-R Shoulder as the scale unit). NOTE: fore-aft displacement resolved in the image plane against the heading, not via MediaPipe Z.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Split Release - The Split - Hands
records.ideal_execution_standard: The hands come up quickly to chest height into a tight, relaxed ready position as the feet land - loaded to strike but not tense.
records.fault_trigger: Hands staying low or arriving late, so the receiver has nothing ready when the defender's hands come. (Finger and grip detail needs the Hand landmarker.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Vertical height of both wrists relative to Sternum, and the speed of their rise into position during the split. Wrists should reach chest / lower-Sternum height. Elbow flexion angle for a tight, compact ready position rather than extended arms.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Split Release - The Split - Head / Eyes
records.ideal_execution_standard: The head stays level and locked on the defender's belt line through the split, with no downward dip toward the feet as the body resets.
records.fault_trigger: Head dropping to watch the feet during the split, losing sight of the defender at the moment the read has to happen. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Head pitch from Nose position relative to the ear midpoint - target is zero downward pitch, the head staying level on the defender's belt line through the split. NOTE: orientation only - actual EYE GAZE is not measurable from the 33-point pose model, and the defender is not in frame in a solo clip, so the target line cannot be confirmed.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Split Release - The Split - Hips
records.ideal_execution_standard: The hips drop the instant the feet land, lowering the centre of gravity immediately so the base is established and loaded in a single motion.
records.fault_trigger: Landing tall and sinking afterwards, so there is a moment where the receiver is upright and unloaded - the split buys no advantage if the hips arrive late.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Vertical drop of Pelvis Center at foot strike, expressed in torso lengths, measured against its pre-split height. The drop should be immediate - coincident with landing rather than following it.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Split Release - The Split - Knees
records.ideal_execution_standard: Both knees bend deep into an athletic squat - roughly 90 to 110 degrees - with weight balanced evenly over the balls of the feet, ready to drive in any direction.
records.fault_trigger: Knees staying too straight to load the split, or weight settling back onto the heels so the receiver cannot push off cleanly.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Bilateral knee flexion angles from the Hip-Knee-Ankle vectors. Reference range 90-110 degrees into an athletic squat. Plus horizontal position of Pelvis Center relative to the Foot Index pair, confirming weight balanced over the balls of the feet. NOTE: the 90-110 range is an uncalibrated starting reference, not a rule.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Split Release - The Split - Shoulders
records.ideal_execution_standard: The shoulders stay perfectly square to the defender through the split, with the torso leaning slightly forward over the knees to shield the chest.
records.fault_trigger: Shoulders rotating during the split, which tips the release direction before the receiver has even read the defender.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Shoulder-line angle (L-R Shoulder vector) relative to the release heading - target is zero rotation, square to the defender. Plus torso lean of the Pelvis-Center-to-Sternum vector, which should tilt slightly forward over the knees. NOTE: squareness resolved as the image-plane shoulder-line angle, not via MediaPipe Z.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Split Release - The Vertical Escape - Footwork
records.ideal_execution_standard: The escape step drives straight upfield on a tight angled path past the defender's hip, clearing their level entirely rather than drifting wide or running into them.
records.fault_trigger: SLAMMING INTO THE DB - releasing directly into the defender's body instead of taking an angled, tight path past their hip. The aim is to clear their frame, not initiate a collision. Also: drifting wide of the track and losing ground. (Defender position is not in frame - path tightness only.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Displacement of the escape step along the release heading, resolved in the image plane, plus the lateral offset of the Pelvis Center path - the track should be tight and angled past the defender's hip rather than wide or into them. NOTE: resolved in the image plane against the heading, not via MediaPipe Z. The defender's hip plane is not in frame in a solo clip, so clearance is inferred from path tightness rather than confirmed.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Split Release - The Vertical Escape - Hands
records.ideal_execution_standard: The trailing arm drives sharply past the shoulder plane with a swift chop, clearing the defender's frame as the receiver locks onto the vertical track.
records.fault_trigger: DROPPING THE HANDS - letting the arms trail behind the body, leaving no protection against a recovering defender's arm bar or jersey pull. (Specific hand technique needs the Hand landmarker.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak velocity of the trailing wrist and elbow, and whether that path passes above the shoulder plane (chop / swipe / club-rip), timed against the escape stride. NOTE: the specific hand technique needs the Hand landmarker; the arm path, height and velocity are measurable from pose.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Split Release - The Vertical Escape - Head / Eyes
records.ideal_execution_standard: The head comes round to track straight upfield, re-establishing vision quickly so the receiver can read coverage depth and locate the football.
records.fault_trigger: Head staying turned toward the release side after the escape, or coming round slowly, so the receiver is late reading coverage and late finding the ball. (Gaze and ball location are not pose-measurable.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) aligning with the upfield heading once the escape is complete, plus the time taken to get there. NOTE: orientation only - actual EYE GAZE is not measurable from the 33-point pose model, and locating the football needs ball tracking.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Split Release - The Vertical Escape - Hips
records.ideal_execution_standard: The hips rotate fully to point straight downfield, locking the receiver onto the vertical track so the route can develop at full speed.
records.fault_trigger: Hips never finishing their rotation, leaving the receiver running at an angle across the field rather than vertically, which costs separation and distorts the route.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Final angle of the hip line (L-R Hip vector) relative to the upfield heading once the escape is complete - target is fully rotated onto the vertical track. Plus the time taken from the plant to reach that alignment.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Split Release - The Vertical Escape - Knees
records.ideal_execution_standard: The outside knee drives high through the escape strides, building linear speed immediately and creating separation from the defender.
records.fault_trigger: Low knee drive out of the escape, so the first strides are short and shuffling and the receiver takes too long to reach full speed.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak vertical height of the outside knee relative to Pelvis Center (knee drive), expressed in torso lengths, across the first strides of the escape.

records.name: WR - Press Release - Split Release - The Vertical Escape - Shoulders
records.ideal_execution_standard: The trailing shoulder rolls inward and away as the receiver clears, eliminating the jersey surface a recovering defender could grab.
records.fault_trigger: Escaping square-shouldered, leaving a full jersey surface exposed for a trailing defender to grab or arm-bar.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Rotation of the shoulder line (L-R Shoulder vector) so the trailing shoulder turns away from the defender's side, reducing the frontal width of the torso. Measured as the image-plane shoulder-line angle relative to the release heading. NOTE: resolved in the image plane, not via MediaPipe Z.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Speed - Bait - Footwork
records.ideal_execution_standard: The feet keep tracking straight under the body along the stem while the upper body begins to turn - the lower body has not yet committed to the break.
records.fault_trigger: Feet drifting off the stem line during the bait, so the lower body commits before the plant and the cut loses its sharpness.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Lateral position of each ankle relative to Pelvis Center during the bait frames - the feet should continue tracking linearly under the body's frame along the stem heading while the upper body rotates above them. Deviation of the ankle path from the stem line is the fault signal.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Speed - Bait - Hands
records.ideal_execution_standard: The arms pull in tight to the body as the turn begins, tightening the frame so the receiver can rotate faster into the break.
records.fault_trigger: Arms staying wide through the bait, slowing the rotation and costing the receiver time in the break. (Finger and grip detail needs the Hand landmarker.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Horizontal distance between each wrist and Sternum across the bait frames - the distance should DECREASE as the arms pull tighter to the frame, reducing the moment of inertia for the rotation.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Speed - Bait - Head / Eyes
records.ideal_execution_standard: The head snaps hard and fast toward the new route trajectory, leading the whole movement - the eyes get there first and the body follows.
records.fault_trigger: BLIND TURNING - head yaw lagging behind the hip and shoulder rotation, meaning the receiver is turning blind rather than leading with his eyes, and will be late seeing the ball. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak angular velocity of head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) toward the new route trajectory. Critically, compare the ONSET FRAME of the head turn against the onset of hip and shoulder rotation - the head must lead. Head yaw lagging behind pelvis or shoulder rotation is the fault signal. NOTE: orientation only - gaze is not pose-measurable.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Speed - Bait - Hips
records.ideal_execution_standard: The hips begin to uncoil toward the break direction, starting the rotation that the plant will complete.
records.fault_trigger: Hips rotating fully before the plant, committing early and letting the defender break on the route; or not uncoiling at all, so the plant has to do all the work and the cut rounds off.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Onset and rate of yaw rotation of the hip line (L-R Hip vector) toward the break direction. The rotation should BEGIN in this phase but remain partial - the full snap happens at the plant. Measured as angular displacement and its timing relative to the head turn.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Speed - Bait - Knees
records.ideal_execution_standard: Both knees stay actively bent through the bait, loaded and ready to handle the high-speed lateral shift that the plant is about to demand.
records.fault_trigger: Knees extending during the bait, so the receiver arrives at the plant unloaded and cannot absorb the lateral force - the cut slips or rounds.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Bilateral knee flexion angles held across the bait frames - both should remain actively flexed rather than extending, ready to absorb the lateral weight shift arriving at the plant.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Speed - Bait - Shoulders
records.ideal_execution_standard: The shoulders turn in time with the head, tilting into the new direction so the upper body initiates the cut and blindsides the defender before the feet move.
records.fault_trigger: Shoulders lagging behind the head turn or staying square, so the upper body does not lead the cut and the transition has to be driven entirely by the plant.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Angular velocity of the shoulder line (L-R Shoulder vector) rotating toward the break, compared against the head's yaw velocity across the same frames - the two should track together. Plus shoulder-line tilt, which creates the deceptive body lean.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Speed - Finish - Footwork
records.ideal_execution_standard: The inside foot drives immediately along the new route line with no drift, no gather step and no wasted movement between the plant and the acceleration.
records.fault_trigger: A gather or recovery step between the plant and the first driving step, or the step drifting off the new line - either way the separation the cut created is handed straight back.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Angle of the first step out of the plant relative to the new route heading, plus lateral deviation of that step from the heading - target is zero drift. Also check for any additional gather or recovery steps between the plant and the first driving step.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Speed - Finish - Hands
records.ideal_execution_standard: The arms fire back into a violent forward pump the moment the cut is made, mechanically driving the receiver back up to sprinting speed.
records.fault_trigger: Arms staying tucked or pumping weakly out of the cut, so the upper body contributes nothing to rebuilding speed on the new line.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak velocity and amplitude of wrist displacement on the first strides out of the cut, compared against the tucked position held at the plant - the arms should re-extend and pump hard immediately.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Speed - Finish - Head / Eyes
records.ideal_execution_standard: The head tracks the target while staying aligned with the new running lane - the receiver finds the ball without letting his body drift off the route line.
records.fault_trigger: Head turning so far to track the ball that the body follows and drifts off the route line, or losing the target entirely coming out of the break. (Gaze and ball location are not pose-measurable.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) held aligned with the new running lane across the exit frames, measured as low angular variance. NOTE: orientation only - actual EYE GAZE is not measurable from the 33-point pose model, and tracking the quarterback or a ball in flight needs ball tracking.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Speed - Finish - Hips
records.ideal_execution_standard: The hips travel on a strict straight line along the new route path, exiting the cut at a sharp angle rather than curving out of it.
records.fault_trigger: ROUNDING THE ANGLE - the pelvis trajectory forms a wide curve instead of a sharp linear exit, giving the defender time and space to recover the separation the cut had created.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Path of Pelvis Center across the frames after the plant, fitted against a straight line along the new route heading. The measurement is the CURVATURE of that path - a sharp linear exit versus a wide arc. Lateral deviation growing over the exit frames is the fault signal.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Speed - Finish - Knees
records.ideal_execution_standard: The lead knee drives high and forward out of the cut, generating maximum instant acceleration back to full speed on the new line.
records.fault_trigger: Low knee drive out of the break, so the receiver shuffles back up to speed and the window the cut opened closes before the ball arrives.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak vertical height of the lead knee relative to Pelvis Center on the first strides out of the cut, expressed in torso lengths, plus the forward component of that knee's travel along the new heading.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Speed - Finish - Shoulders
records.ideal_execution_standard: The shoulders square up to the new route line and the torso resumes its forward sprinting lean, the body reset into pure acceleration.
records.fault_trigger: Shoulders staying rotated or the torso staying upright after the cut, so the receiver runs out of the break unbalanced and slow to rebuild speed.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Shoulder-line angle (L-R Shoulder vector) relative to the new route heading - should return to square. Plus the Spine vector angle relative to vertical, which should resume its aggressive forward sprint lean after the inward tilt of the plant.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Speed - Load - Footwork
records.ideal_execution_standard: Stride length holds at its full stem value through the load step while the weight quietly prepares to transfer laterally - nothing shortens or gathers.
records.fault_trigger: Stride shortening on the load step, which is a visible gather and tells the defender the break is one step away.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Stride length on the load step compared against the stem's stride length - it should be maintained, not shortened. Plus lateral position of the landing foot relative to Pelvis Center, indicating weight beginning to prepare for the lateral transfer.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Speed - Load - Hands
records.ideal_execution_standard: The arm pump continues exactly as it was through the stem - unchanged amplitude and rhythm, so nothing about the upper body signals the load.
records.fault_trigger: Arm mechanics changing during the load step - shortening, tightening or breaking rhythm - which gives the defender a visual cue that the break is imminent.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Amplitude and frequency of wrist displacement across the load step, compared against their stem values - both should be unchanged. Any deviation is a visual tell.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Speed - Load - Head / Eyes
records.ideal_execution_standard: Vision stays fixed downfield right through the load step, holding the deep threat until the exact frame the transition begins.
records.fault_trigger: Head beginning to turn during the load step rather than at the transition, breaking the deception one step too early. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) held at zero relative to the stem heading through the load step, with rotation beginning only at the transition frame. The measurement is the TIMING of the first head movement relative to the load step's ground contact. NOTE: orientation only - gaze is not pose-measurable.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Speed - Load - Hips
records.ideal_execution_standard: The hips drop a small, controlled amount to load the cut - without losing any forward speed. The sink is subtle enough that the defender cannot see it coming.
records.fault_trigger: POPPING UP - a sudden upward spike in hip or chest height, destroying the low sprint angle and broadcasting the break. Also: sinking so far that forward velocity drops and the cut becomes a gather.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Vertical drop of Pelvis Center on the load step, expressed in torso lengths - a small controlled drop (roughly an inch on an adult frame). Critically, cross-check forward velocity across the same window: it must NOT decrease. An upward spike in Pelvis Center or Sternum height is the fault signal.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Speed - Load - Knees
records.ideal_execution_standard: The lead knee bends more deeply on the load step, absorbing the downward force of the sink while keeping the receiver stable at full speed.
records.fault_trigger: Lead knee staying stiff through the load step, so the sink cannot be absorbed and the receiver either pops up or loses balance going into the plant.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Knee flexion angle of the lead leg at ground contact on the load step, compared against its stem values - flexion should INCREASE to absorb the downward force while the body stays at speed.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Speed - Load - Shoulders
records.ideal_execution_standard: The shoulders stay completely square to the stem and forward over the knees during the load - the upper body reveals nothing while the lower body prepares.
records.fault_trigger: Shoulders starting to rotate toward the break during the load step, an early tell that lets the defender jump the route.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Shoulder-line angle (L-R Shoulder vector) relative to the stem heading - target is zero rotational deviation. Plus horizontal position of the shoulder midpoint relative to the knees, which should stay forward over them.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Speed - Preparation - Footwork
records.ideal_execution_standard: Stride length stays maximal and constant through the vertical stem - the receiver runs at genuine top speed so the deep route is believable right up to the break.
records.fault_trigger: STUTTER STEPPING - stride length shortening or step frequency rising before the break point, which tells the defender a cut is coming and surrenders the advantage the stem was built to create.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Stride length per step along the stem heading, expressed in shoulder widths (L-R Shoulder as the scale unit), plus step frequency. Both should hold constant at their top-speed values through the stem. A reduction in stride length OR an increase in step frequency before the break point is the fault signal. NOTE: resolved in the image plane against the stem heading, not via MediaPipe Z.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Speed - Preparation - Hands
records.ideal_execution_standard: The arms pump at full amplitude past the ribcage throughout the stem, driving the sprint and giving no indication a break is coming.
records.fault_trigger: Arm pump shortening or slowing during the stem, an early visual tell that the receiver is about to break.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Amplitude of wrist displacement front-to-back past the ribcage frame, plus pump frequency, held constant through the stem. Cross-check contralateral timing against the legs.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Speed - Preparation - Head / Eyes
records.ideal_execution_standard: The head stays locked straight downfield through the stem, selling the vertical route and giving the defender nothing to read.
records.fault_trigger: Head turning toward the break direction during the stem, tipping the route before the receiver has reached the break point. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) held at zero relative to the stem heading, measured as low angular variance across the stem frames. NOTE: orientation only - actual EYE GAZE is not measurable from the 33-point pose model.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Speed - Preparation - Hips
records.ideal_execution_standard: The hips carry constant high-speed forward travel with minimal vertical bounce - all the energy goes into covering ground down the stem.
records.fault_trigger: Velocity dropping off during the stem, or excessive vertical bounce wasting energy - either way the deep threat is not sold and the defender does not have to respect it.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Forward velocity of Pelvis Center along the stem heading, held constant at top speed, plus vertical oscillation of Pelvis Center measured as variance in torso lengths - minimal bounce indicates efficient top-end running.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Speed - Preparation - Knees
records.ideal_execution_standard: The front knee lifts high through the swing phase on every stride, sustaining genuine top-end speed down the stem.
records.fault_trigger: Knee lift dropping off during the stem, which slows the receiver and signals that he is preparing to break rather than running deep.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak vertical height of the swinging knee relative to Pelvis Center on each stride, expressed in torso lengths. Should hold at top-speed values through the stem rather than dropping off.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Speed - Preparation - Shoulders
records.ideal_execution_standard: The torso holds an aggressive forward lean over the toes through the stem, matching what a genuine deep sprint looks like.
records.fault_trigger: Torso rising toward upright during the stem, which reads as a receiver preparing to stop rather than one running past the defender.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Angle of the Spine vector (Pelvis Center to Sternum) relative to vertical, held at an acute forward lean through the stem. Cross-check against the hip-to-knee vector to confirm a whole-body sprint lean rather than folding at the waist.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Speed - Strike - Footwork
records.ideal_execution_standard: The outside cutting foot lands with the toe already pointed along the new route path, steering the body into the break rather than braking against it. The toe is pulled up into dorsiflexion so the heel bites the grass first, giving clean, firm contact instead of a slide or a stubbed toe. The step stays compact and lands directly beneath the centre of mass - no over-extending or lunging - which preserves body control and keeps the defender believing the receiver is still running vertically until the instant the weight drops.
records.fault_trigger: THE BLIND PLANT - the foot lands still pointing straight downfield instead of along the new path, so the receiver slides outward, loses his base, and the cut becomes a skid rather than a redirect. Toe left down (plantarflexed) rather than pulled up, so the receiver slides through the plant or stubs the toe instead of biting the ground heel-first. Over-extending or lunging the plant step out ahead of the centre of mass, which costs body control and tips the break early.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] THREE signals at the plant frame. (1) TOE DIRECTION: Heel-to-Foot-Index vector of the plant foot compared against the angle of the new route path - the two should align. A plant foot still pointing along the old stem heading is the fault signal, and shows up as lateral ankle slide after contact. (2) DORSIFLEXION: angle between the Foot-Index-to-Heel vector and the Ankle-to-Knee (shin) vector - the toe should be pulled UP so the heel contacts first. Check which of Heel or Foot Index reaches its lowest vertical position first at touchdown: heel-first is correct. (3) STEP COMPACTNESS: horizontal position of the plant ankle relative to Pelvis Center at contact - the foot should land directly beneath the centre of mass, not reaching ahead of it. Cross-check horizontal ankle velocity at strike for slide.
records.coaching_cue: Toe up, heel first - plant under yourself, don't reach.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Speed - Strike - Hands
records.ideal_execution_standard: The arms stay tucked tight to the chest through the plant, keeping the frame compact so the body rotates as fast as possible into the new direction.
records.fault_trigger: Arms flying wide at the plant, slowing the rotation and costing time in the break - and often unbalancing the receiver as he exits. (Finger and grip detail needs the Hand landmarker.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Distance from each wrist to Sternum at the plant frame, expressed in torso lengths - should be at its minimum across the whole cut, the arms tucked tight to maximise rotational speed.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Speed - Strike - Head / Eyes
records.ideal_execution_standard: By the plant the head is fully locked down the new route corridor, already looking for open space and the football before the body has finished turning.
records.fault_trigger: Head still rotating at the plant rather than already locked on the new corridor, so the receiver comes out of the cut late to find the ball. (Gaze and ball location are not pose-measurable.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) fully aligned with the new route corridor by the plant frame, and held there. The measurement is whether the rotation is COMPLETE at the plant rather than still in progress. NOTE: orientation only - gaze is not pose-measurable, and spotting the football needs ball tracking.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Speed - Strike - Hips
records.ideal_execution_standard: The hips snap open to exactly the angle the head and the plant foot have already established - head, foot and hips all pointing down the same new route line.
records.fault_trigger: Hips opening to a different angle than the head and plant foot, so the body fights itself through the cut and the exit line is wrong.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Final angle of the hip line (L-R Hip vector) at and immediately after the plant, compared against the head yaw angle and the plant foot's toe direction - all three should converge on the same new heading. Divergence between them is the fault signal.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Speed - Strike - Knees
records.ideal_execution_standard: The plant knee drops into deep flexion at contact, loading the leg as a high-speed spring that will fire the receiver out on the new line.
records.fault_trigger: Planting on a stiff leg, which cannot absorb the speed or store energy - the receiver either slides through the cut or has to take recovery steps before accelerating.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Knee flexion angle of the planting leg at ground contact from the Hip-Knee-Ankle vector - should drop into acute flexion to load the leg as a spring. Plus the rate of that flexion, which indicates how much force is being absorbed and stored.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Speed - Strike - Shoulders
records.ideal_execution_standard: The torso tilts sharply inward toward the new route angle at the plant, countering the centrifugal force of the cut and keeping the receiver balanced through the turn.
records.fault_trigger: Staying upright through the plant, so momentum carries the receiver wide and the cut rounds off; or over-leaning and losing balance out of the break.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Lateral tilt of the Spine vector (Pelvis Center to Sternum) toward the inside of the new route angle at the plant, measured in the image plane. The lean counters centrifugal force - too little and the receiver is carried wide, too much and he loses balance.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Bait - Footwork
records.ideal_execution_standard: The wide, low stance holds for a beat as forward velocity reaches zero - the receiver is genuinely stopped, not still drifting.
records.fault_trigger: Still carrying forward velocity through the pause, so the receiver drifts past the break point and the route depth is wrong; or the base narrowing and losing the platform for the plant.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Forward velocity of Pelvis Center reaching zero, plus ankle separation held at its wide breakdown value and positional variance of both ankles across the pause frames. The measurement is a genuine momentary stop on a wide base, not a slow drift through.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Bait - Hands
records.ideal_execution_standard: The hands stay elevated and active in a compact frame through the pause, ready to catch and tight enough not to slow the rotation.
records.fault_trigger: Hands dropping or going wide during the pause, so the receiver is neither ready for a quick throw nor compact enough to turn fast. (Finger and grip detail needs the Hand landmarker.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Vertical height of both wrists relative to Sternum held elevated across the pause, plus distance from each wrist to Sternum staying compact. Active hands show as small continuous motion rather than being frozen or dropped.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Bait - Head / Eyes
records.ideal_execution_standard: The head snaps immediately and fast toward the new route, leading the movement so the eyes find the quarterback before the body has finished turning.
records.fault_trigger: BLIND TURN - the torso rotates before the eyes do, so the receiver comes out of the break without having found the ball and is late reacting to a throw already in the air. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak angular velocity of head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) toward the new route. Critically, compare the ONSET FRAME of the head turn against the onset of shoulder and hip rotation - the head must lead. Torso rotating before the head is the fault signal. NOTE: orientation only - gaze is not pose-measurable.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Bait - Hips
records.ideal_execution_standard: The hips hold their low position through the pause, staying loaded so the plant can fire without needing to re-sink.
records.fault_trigger: Hips rising during the pause, unloading the legs - the receiver then has to drop again before he can drive out, and the break is late.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Vertical height of Pelvis Center held at its low breakdown value across the pause frames, expressed in torso lengths - no upward drift while the upper body initiates the turn.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Bait - Knees
records.ideal_execution_standard: The deep knee bend is maintained through the pause, keeping the lower body loaded like a spring ready to fire on the plant.
records.fault_trigger: Knees extending during the pause, so the stored energy leaks away and the drive out has to be generated from scratch.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Bilateral knee flexion angles held at their deep breakdown values across the pause frames - maintained, not extending. The measurement is stability of the angle over the window.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Bait - Shoulders
records.ideal_execution_standard: The shoulders rotate in behind the head turn, shifting the body's equilibrium toward the new break so the plant can redirect immediately.
records.fault_trigger: Shoulders rotating before or without the head, so the body commits blind and the receiver is late picking up the ball out of the break.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Angular velocity of the shoulder line (L-R Shoulder vector) rotating toward the new break direction, compared against head yaw velocity across the same frames - the shoulders should FOLLOW the head, not lead it.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Finish - Footwork
records.ideal_execution_standard: The receiver pushes explosively off the instep of the plant foot into a low, linear first step - the anchor converts straight into acceleration with nothing wasted.
records.fault_trigger: A gather step between the plant and the drive out, or a high, short first step - either way the stored energy is wasted and the defender recovers the separation the stop created.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Contact time of the plant foot from strike to toe-off (shorter is better), plus the height and length of the first step out along the new heading - it should be low and linear rather than high or rounded. Also check for any gather step between the plant and the first driving step.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Finish - Hands
records.ideal_execution_standard: The arms fire back into a violent punch-like pump the instant the drive out begins, mechanically restoring sprint momentum from a standing stop.
records.fault_trigger: Arms staying compact or pumping weakly out of the break, so the upper body adds nothing to rebuilding speed from a dead stop - where it matters most.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak velocity and amplitude of wrist displacement on the first strides out of the break, compared against the compact position held through the breakdown and pause - the arms should re-extend into a hard punch-like pump immediately.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Finish - Head / Eyes
records.ideal_execution_standard: Vision stays locked on the quarterback through the drive out, tracking the throw while the body holds its line on the new trajectory.
records.fault_trigger: Losing the quarterback coming out of the break, or turning the head so far that the body follows and the exit line curves off the route. (Gaze and ball location are not pose-measurable.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) held on the target across the exit frames, measured as low angular variance, while the Pelvis Center path stays linear.
