The measurement is the head tracking the target WITHOUT the body following it off the route line. NOTE: orientation only - gaze and ball location are not pose-measurable.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Finish - Hips
records.ideal_execution_standard: The hips rotate rapidly to sit parallel with the new exit trajectory, locking the receiver onto a sharp straight line out of the break.
records.fault_trigger: ROUNDING - the exit trajectory curves rather than forming a sharp line, so the defender recovers the ground the stop had won. Usually caused by the hips rotating too slowly out of the plant.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Angular velocity of the hip line (L-R Hip vector) rotating to align parallel with the new exit trajectory, plus the time taken from the plant to reach that alignment. Additionally, path of Pelvis Center across the exit frames fitted against a straight line - the CURVATURE of that path is the rounding measurement.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Finish - Knees
records.ideal_execution_standard: The lead knee drives immediately up and forward out of the plant, converting the stored energy into instant acceleration on the new line.
records.fault_trigger: Low knee drive out of the break, so the receiver shuffles back up to speed and the throwing window closes before he can separate.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak vertical height of the lead knee relative to Pelvis Center on the first strides out of the break, expressed in torso lengths, plus the forward component of that knee's travel along the new heading.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Finish - Shoulders
records.ideal_execution_standard: The shoulders square up to the new path and the torso resumes its forward sprint lean, the body reset from stopping posture into pure acceleration.
records.fault_trigger: Shoulders staying rotated or the torso staying upright and tucked after the break, so the receiver runs out slow and unbalanced on the new line.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Shoulder-line angle (L-R Shoulder vector) relative to the new exit heading - should square up rapidly. Plus the Spine vector angle relative to vertical, which should return to a forward sprint lean after the tucked breakdown posture.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Load - Footwork
records.ideal_execution_standard: Stride shortens rapidly into 2 to 3 chop steps, gathering the feet underneath the body to kill momentum in as little ground as possible.
records.fault_trigger: Too many chop steps, or a gradual slow-down rather than a sharp gather - the breakdown takes too long and the defender closes the space before the break.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Stride length across the breakdown steps, expressed in shoulder widths, compared against the stem values - it should drop sharply across 2 to 3 chop steps. Plus step frequency, which should rise correspondingly. The measurement is the RATE of the shortening: abrupt is correct, gradual is telegraphing.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Load - Hands
records.ideal_execution_standard: The violent sprint pump compacts into a tight position near the chest, quieting the arms so they do not fight the deceleration or unbalance the body.
records.fault_trigger: Arms still swinging wide through the breakdown, throwing the receiver off balance at exactly the moment he needs to be stable. (Finger and grip detail needs the Hand landmarker.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Amplitude of wrist displacement across the breakdown steps compared against the stem values - should drop sharply as the arms compact toward the chest. Plus distance from each wrist to Sternum, which should decrease.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Load - Head / Eyes
records.ideal_execution_standard: Vision stays locked downfield through the breakdown steps, holding the deep threat even as the body gathers to stop.
records.fault_trigger: Head turning during the breakdown rather than at the visual snap, giving the defender an extra beat of warning before the break. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Head yaw held at zero relative to the stem heading across the breakdown frames, with rotation beginning only at the visual snap. The measurement is the TIMING of the first head movement relative to the chop steps. NOTE: orientation only - gaze is not pose-measurable.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Load - Hips
records.ideal_execution_standard: The hips drop drastically on the breakdown steps, dumping the centre of gravity low so the legs can absorb the speed and the body can anchor.
records.fault_trigger: STIFF LEG - entering the breakdown with the hips still high, so the deceleration is absorbed through the knees rather than the whole lower body. Slower to stop and hard on the joints.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Vertical drop of Pelvis Center across the breakdown steps, expressed in torso lengths - a drastic sink relative to its stem height. Pelvis Center remaining high on entry to the breakdown is the fault signal, and correlates with insufficient knee flexion.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Load - Knees
records.ideal_execution_standard: Both knees move from maximum sprint drive into deep bilateral flexion, working as shock absorbers to soak up the speed the stem built.
records.fault_trigger: Knees staying relatively straight through the breakdown, so there is nothing to absorb the momentum - the receiver skids, stumbles, or needs extra steps to stop.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Bilateral knee flexion angles across the breakdown steps, compared against their stem values - both should transition from sprint drive angles into deep flexion, acting as shock absorbers. The measurement is the magnitude and speed of that transition.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Load - Shoulders
records.ideal_execution_standard: The forward sprint lean shifts back into a tucked, balanced position with the shoulders inside the knee frame, so the receiver can anchor rather than being carried forward.
records.fault_trigger: Shoulders staying out over the toes through the breakdown, so momentum carries the chest forward and the receiver cannot stop cleanly or has to take recovery steps.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Angle of the Spine vector relative to vertical, transitioning from the stem's forward sprint lean to a more upright tucked position. Plus horizontal position of the shoulder midpoint relative to the knees - the shoulders should come back inside the knee frame rather than staying out over the toes.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Preparation - Footwork
records.ideal_execution_standard: Stride length stays maximal through the vertical stem, holding genuine top speed so the deep threat forces the defender to turn and run.
records.fault_trigger: TELEGRAPHING - stride shortening or velocity dropping before the breakdown, which warns the defender the receiver is about to stop and lets them sit on the route.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Stride length per step along the stem heading, expressed in shoulder widths (L-R Shoulder as the scale unit), held constant at top-speed values through the stem. Any early reduction in stride length, or a drop in Pelvis Center forward velocity before the breakdown begins, is the fault signal.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Preparation - Hands
records.ideal_execution_standard: The arms pump violently through the stem at full sprint amplitude, driving the vertical push and giving no hint the break is coming.
records.fault_trigger: Arm pump shortening or slowing during the stem, a visual tell that the receiver is about to break down.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Amplitude and frequency of wrist displacement front-to-back through the stem, held at full sprint values. Cross-check contralateral timing against the legs.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Preparation - Head / Eyes
records.ideal_execution_standard: Vision stays locked straight downfield through the stem, maintaining the deep vertical threat that makes the stop work.
records.fault_trigger: Head turning toward the break during the stem, breaking the vertical threat before the receiver has reached the break point. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) held at zero relative to the stem heading, measured as low angular variance across the stem frames. NOTE: orientation only - gaze is not pose-measurable.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Preparation - Hips
records.ideal_execution_standard: The hips carry constant high-speed travel down the stem with minimal bounce, selling the vertical route before anything changes.
records.fault_trigger: Velocity easing off during the stem, so the deep threat is never established and the defender does not have to respect it.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Forward velocity of Pelvis Center along the stem heading, held constant at top speed, plus vertical oscillation measured as variance in torso lengths.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Preparation - Knees
records.ideal_execution_standard: The knees drive at full sprint height through the stem, generating the maximum speed that the breakdown will then have to absorb.
records.fault_trigger: Knee drive dropping off during the stem, slowing the receiver early and removing the vertical threat the stop cut depends on.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak vertical height of the swinging knee relative to Pelvis Center on each stride, expressed in torso lengths, sustained at top-speed values through the stem.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Preparation - Shoulders
records.ideal_execution_standard: The torso holds an aggressive forward sprint lean through the stem, the posture of a receiver running past the defender rather than one preparing to stop.
records.fault_trigger: Torso rising toward upright during the stem, an early tell that the receiver is preparing to break down.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Angle of the Spine vector (Pelvis Center to Sternum) relative to vertical, held at an acute forward sprint lean through the stem. Cross-check against the hip-to-knee vector to confirm whole-body lean rather than waist flexion.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Strike - Footwork
records.ideal_execution_standard: The outside foot lands with the toe pointing exactly down the new route angle, acting as a steering mechanism rather than just a brake. The toe is pulled up into dorsiflexion so the heel bites the grass first, giving clean, firm contact instead of a slide or a stubbed toe. The step stays compact and lands directly beneath the centre of mass - no over-extending or lunging - which both preserves body control and keeps the defender believing the receiver is still accelerating vertically until the instant the weight drops.
records.fault_trigger: BLIND PLANT - the toe points straight ahead or wide of the new path, so the foot brakes instead of steering and the receiver slips off the anchor. Toe left down (plantarflexed) rather than pulled up, so the receiver slides through the plant or stubs the toe instead of biting the ground heel-first. Over-extending or lunging the plant step out ahead of the centre of mass, which costs body control and tips the break early by showing the defender the receiver is gathering rather than still running.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] THREE signals at the plant frame. (1) TOE DIRECTION: Heel-to-Foot-Index vector of the plant foot compared against the new route path angle - the two should align. (2) DORSIFLEXION: angle between the Foot-Index-to-Heel vector and the Ankle-to-Knee (shin) vector - the toe should be pulled UP so the heel contacts first. Check which of Heel or Foot Index reaches its lowest vertical position first at touchdown: heel-first is correct. (3) STEP COMPACTNESS: horizontal position of the plant ankle relative to Pelvis Center at contact - the foot should land directly beneath the centre of mass, not reaching ahead of it. Cross-check horizontal ankle velocity at strike for slide.
records.coaching_cue: Toe up, heel first - plant under yourself, don't reach.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Strike - Head / Eyes
records.ideal_execution_standard: The head snap lands on exactly the same instant as the cleat hits the ground - eyes and anchor arriving together, so the receiver is looking at the quarterback the moment he is able to catch.
records.fault_trigger: Head snap arriving before or after cleat impact rather than with it - either the receiver tips the break early, or he is still turning when the ball is already on its way.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Frame at which head yaw rotation completes, compared against the frame of the plant foot's ground contact - the two should coincide. The measurement is SYNCHRONISATION between the head snap and cleat impact, measured in frames of offset. NOTE: orientation only - gaze is not pose-measurable.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Strike - Hips
records.ideal_execution_standard: The hips reach their lowest point of the entire cut at the plant - the core locked down against the ground, giving the anchor maximum stability.
records.fault_trigger: Hips already rising at the plant rather than bottoming out, so the anchor is weak and the receiver gets carried past the break point.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Vertical height of Pelvis Center at the plant frame, expressed in torso lengths - should reach its absolute minimum across the whole cut. The measurement is the lowest point of the entire movement occurring at the plant, not before or after it.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Strike - Knees
records.ideal_execution_standard: The planting knee flexes deep at contact, building a powerful stopping platform that absorbs the last of the momentum and stores it for the drive out.
records.fault_trigger: Planting on a straight or shallow-bent leg, which cannot absorb the remaining momentum - the receiver skids through the break or jars to a stop with nothing stored for the exit.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Knee flexion angle of the planting leg at ground contact from the Hip-Knee-Ankle vector - should reach deep flexion to create a stopping platform. Plus the rate of flexion, which indicates how much force is being absorbed.

records.name: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Strike - Shoulders
records.ideal_execution_standard: The torso leans securely out over the planting toe, keeping the weight stacked over the anchor so the receiver does not slip backward off the plant.
records.fault_trigger: Shoulders sitting back behind the plant foot, so the weight is behind the anchor and the receiver slips backward instead of driving out.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Horizontal position of the shoulder midpoint relative to the plant foot's Foot Index at ground contact - the shoulders should sit over or slightly ahead of the planting toe. Shoulders falling behind the plant foot is the fault signal and correlates with backward slippage.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Comeback - Finish
records.ideal_execution_standard: Drive powerfully off the inside instep of the directing foot and work back downhill toward the ball, shortening the distance of the throw, squaring the shoulders to the quarterback to shield the ball, and securing the catch with the hands extended away from the frame.
records.fault_trigger: WAITING ON THE BALL - standing still after making the cut. The receiver must actively run back downhill toward the ball to stop a trailing defender undercutting the route for an interception. (Ball position and defender leverage are not pose-measurable.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Displacement of Pelvis Center after the plant, resolved along the 45-degree downhill vector in the image plane - the fault signal is near-zero displacement (standing still) after the break. Plus the shoulder line squaring to the new heading, and horizontal distance of both wrists from Sternum increasing at the catch point (hands extended away from the frame). NOTE: whether the receiver actually shortened the throw or shielded a defender needs the ball and the defender in frame.
records.coaching_cue: Come back to the ball - never wait on it.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Comeback - Power Plant
records.ideal_execution_standard: As the eyes find the quarterback, drive the outside cutting foot down into a tight, compact step directly under the hips. The toe is pulled up sharply into dorsiflexion right before contact, striking heel and midfoot first to lock the brakes instantly. Pivot and direct the toe at a 45-degree angle back down the stem toward the sideline.
records.fault_trigger: THE LUNGING TOE PLANT - reaching too far forward with the planting step and letting the toe point downward before contact. This strips core stability, causes a slide, and tips off the defender early because the running stride visibly changes before the cut.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] THREE signals at the plant frame. (1) COMPACTNESS: horizontal distance between the plant ankle and Pelvis Center - the foot must land directly under the frame, not out in front of the chest. (2) DORSIFLEXION / STRIKE ORDER: the Heel must reach its lowest vertical position BEFORE the Foot Index at touchdown (heel/midfoot first), with the Foot-Index-to-Heel vector showing the toe pulled up against the shin. A toe-first strike is the fault signal. (3) TOE DIRECTION: Heel-to-Foot-Index vector pointing back down the stem line at roughly 45 degrees toward the sideline.
records.coaching_cue: Heel first, under your frame - point it back at 45.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Comeback - Stem & Load
records.ideal_execution_standard: Explode off the line and sprint at full vertical velocity for 12-15 yards, forcing the defender to turn their hips into a deep, desperate retreat. At break depth, violently sink the hips and chop the cleats rapidly into the turf - the sudden lowering of the centre of gravity is the braking system that halts forward momentum.
records.fault_trigger: STIFF-LEGGED BRAKING - trying to stop without sinking the hips. The receiver stumbles forward, takes too many recovery steps, and puts dangerous stress on the knees. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference and the declared route.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Vertical drop of Pelvis Center at the break, expressed in torso lengths - should be a violent sink relative to its stem height, coinciding with the chop steps. Cross-check bilateral knee flexion: if the hips stay high while the knees absorb the braking force, that is the stiff-leg fault. Break depth target 12-15 yards. NOTE: absolute depth needs a scale reference (player height) and the route declared; without them, report the measured depth without judging it. Detailed breakdown mechanics are held in Cuts - Stop.
records.coaching_cue: Sink your butt - don't brake with your knees.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Comeback - Visual Snap
records.ideal_execution_standard: The millisecond forward momentum halts, snap the head and eyes back around over the inside shoulder to face the quarterback first. Turning the vision inside opens the upper torso and picks up the ball's trajectory before the lower body has finished its pivot.
records.fault_trigger: Head coming round late or after the body has pivoted, so the receiver finishes the break without having found the quarterback - and a ball already in the air arrives before he is looking for it. (Gaze and ball location are not pose-measurable.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Total angular change and peak velocity of head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) rotating back over the inside shoulder toward the quarterback - approaching a 180 degree reversal. Critically, the FRAME at which the rotation begins compared against the frame forward velocity reaches zero, and against the plant contact - the head must lead both. NOTE: orientation only - locating the quarterback and the ball is not confirmable from pose.
records.coaching_cue: The instant you stop - find the quarterback.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Corner - Angle Plant
records.ideal_execution_standard: As the eyes lock onto the pylon, drive the INSIDE foot down into a tight, compact step directly under the centre of mass. The toe is pulled up sharply into dorsiflexion right before contact, striking with a rigid foot. Instantly point the toe down a 45-degree track toward the corner, masking the break until the last possible instant.
records.fault_trigger: THE LUNGING SLIDE - lunging too far forward with a loose, downward-pointing toe. The over-extension lacks the rigidity to anchor a 45-degree turn, so the shoe slides over the grass and the defender closes the gap.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] THREE signals at the plant frame, on the INSIDE foot. (1) COMPACTNESS: displacement between the plant ankle and Pelvis Center along the stem heading - the foot must land directly under the centre of mass, not reaching ahead of it. High separation is the lunging fault. (2) DORSIFLEXION: angle between the Foot-Index-to-Heel vector and the Ankle-to-Knee shin vector - toe pulled UP pre-impact, heel reaching its lowest vertical point before the Foot Index. (3) TOE DIRECTION: Heel-to-Foot-Index vector pivoting to 45 degrees OUTWARD toward the corner relative to the stem heading.
records.coaching_cue: Toe up, under yourself, point it at the corner.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Corner - Finish
records.ideal_execution_standard: Push violently off the inside instep of the directing foot, flip the hips wide open, and punch the outside arm across the body to accelerate along a strict 45-degree line toward the corner.
records.fault_trigger: FLATTENING THE ANGLE - letting the route angle flat toward the sideline rather than holding a strict 45 degrees toward the corner pylon, which shortens the route and lets the defender close.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Angle of the Pelvis Center exit trajectory relative to the stem heading - target is a strict 45 degrees toward the corner, held linear. The fault signal is that angle opening toward 90 degrees (flattening toward the sideline). Plus horizontal displacement of the outside wrist across the Sternum midline, confirming the cross-body arm punch. NOTE: resolved in the image plane against the stem heading.
records.coaching_cue: Hold 45 to the pylon - don't flatten out.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Corner - Stem & Load
records.ideal_execution_standard: Drive off the line at full velocity for 10-12 yards (12-15 on the deeper variation) with pads leaning forward and long natural strides, pushing the defender into a deep vertical retreat. One step before the break, subtly drop the hips an inch to gather balance and prepare the core for high-speed redirection - without chopping or stutter-stepping.
records.fault_trigger: FADING EARLY - unconsciously drifting outward toward the sideline before the break depth, alerting the defender to clamp down on the corner. Also: chopping or stutter-stepping into the load, which turns a speed cut into a visible breakdown. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference and the called depth.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Linear displacement of Pelvis Center and the ankle path along the stem heading, resolved in the image plane - the fault signal is lateral drift toward the sideline accumulating BEFORE the break point. Plus a subtle vertical drop of Pelvis Center (roughly an inch on an adult frame) one step before the break, WITHOUT any reduction in stride length or step frequency - this is a speed-cut load, not a breakdown. Break depth 10-12 yards standard; a deeper variation runs 12-15. NOTE: absolute depth needs a scale reference (player height) and the called depth; without them, report the measured depth without judging it. Detailed mechanics are held in Cuts - Speed.
records.coaching_cue: Straight up the track - sink an inch, don't chop.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Corner - Visual Snap
records.ideal_execution_standard: At break depth, snap the head and eyes sharply toward the corner pylon first. The rapid visual rotation opens the upper torso and shifts equilibrium toward the outside before the lower body begins to pivot.
records.fault_trigger: Head turning with the plant or after it rather than leading it, so the torso never pre-rotates and the break is slower and squarer than it should be. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak angular velocity of head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) toward the corner, and critically the FRAME at which that rotation begins compared against the plant foot's ground-contact frame - the head must lead the plant. NOTE: orientation only - actual EYE GAZE is not measurable, and the pylon is not in frame in a solo clip, so only the direction and timing of the turn are assessable.
records.coaching_cue: Eyes to the pylon first - then the foot.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Cross - Angle Plant
records.ideal_execution_standard: The instant the eyes find the cross lane, drive the outside foot down into a sharp, compact step positioned firmly beneath the body weight. The toe is pulled up before the foot strikes to ground cleanly. Instantly point the toe and direct the final step down a flat 90-degree track across the field, masking the horizontal break until the last possible instant.
records.fault_trigger: THE DOWNFIELD TOE PLANT - planting with the toe still pointing toward the end zone. Failing to direct the foot at 90 degrees causes the receiver to drift downfield, running straight into the waiting linebackers.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] THREE signals at the plant frame, on the OUTSIDE foot. (1) COMPACTNESS: horizontal position of the plant ankle relative to Pelvis Center - the cleat must land firmly beneath the body weight, not reaching ahead. (2) DORSIFLEXION: angle between the Foot-Index-to-Heel vector and the Ankle-to-Knee shin vector - the toe pulled up before the foot strikes, grounding the receiver cleanly. (3) TOE DIRECTION: Heel-to-Foot-Index vector pivoting to a flat 90 degrees inward across the formation relative to the release heading. A Foot Index still pointing along the release heading is the primary fault signal.
records.coaching_cue: Point the toe across - not at the end zone.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Cross - Finish
records.ideal_execution_standard: Push violently off the inside instep of the directing foot, sprint flat along the line across the formation, snap the eyes back over the inside shoulder to look for the ball, and secure the catch while bracing to turn upfield.
records.fault_trigger: BUBBLING THE ROUTE - letting the route angle backward toward the line of scrimmage or bubble downfield. The line must stay flat and parallel to the line of scrimmage to maximise the open void. (Ball location needs ball tracking.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Angle of the Pelvis Center exit trajectory relative to the release heading - target is a flat 90 degrees held linear across the field. The fault signal is any component of that trajectory travelling either forward downfield or backward toward the line of scrimmage (curvature in the path). Plus head yaw snapping back over the inside shoulder after the break, and horizontal displacement of the outside wrist across the Sternum midline confirming the cross-body punch. NOTE: resolved in the image plane; ball location needs ball tracking.
records.coaching_cue: Flat across the field - no bubble.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Cross - Stem & Load
records.ideal_execution_standard: Explode vertically off the line for 2 to 3 hard steps, driving the pads forward to threaten the defender's leverage and make them respect the go route. Then prepare to redirect sideways by subtly sinking the hips, keeping the feet moving at full speed with no choppy or gathering steps.
records.fault_trigger: FADING EARLY - drifting inward toward the middle of the field right off the snap. This tells the defender exactly where the receiver is going and lets them squeeze him into the linebacker level. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Count and displacement of the vertical acceleration steps along the release heading - target 2 to 3 explosive steps before the break, resolved in the image plane. The fault signal is lateral drift toward the middle beginning immediately off the line rather than after the vertical steps. Plus a subtle vertical drop of Pelvis Center WITHOUT any reduction in stride length or step frequency - a speed-cut load, not a breakdown. Break depth 1-3 yards. NOTE: absolute depth needs a scale reference; without it, report the measured depth without judging it. Detailed mechanics are held in Cuts - Speed.
records.coaching_cue: Two hard steps vertical first - don't drift off the line.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Cross - Visual Snap
records.ideal_execution_standard: At break depth, snap the head and eyes sharply across the formation first. The visual focus locks onto the open grass underneath the linebackers, which naturally uncoils the neck and shoulders into the cross lane.
records.fault_trigger: Head turning with the plant or after it rather than leading it, so the shoulders never uncoil into the lane and the receiver crosses without having seen the linebacker level. (Gaze and defender positions are not pose-measurable.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak angular velocity of head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) rotating across the formation, and the FRAME at which that rotation begins compared against the plant foot's ground-contact frame - the head must lead. Plus shoulder-line rotation following the head (the neck and shoulders uncoiling into the cross lane). NOTE: orientation only - whether the receiver actually located open grass under the linebackers cannot be confirmed from a solo clip.
records.coaching_cue: Eyes across first - find the grass under the backers.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Curl - Finish
records.ideal_execution_standard: Drive powerfully off the inside instep of the directing foot, open the chest completely to the quarterback, work back downhill toward the ball to shorten the distance of the throw, and secure the catch with the hands extended away from the frame.
records.fault_trigger: WAITING ON THE BALL - standing still after making the cut. The receiver must actively run back downhill toward the ball to stop a trailing defender undercutting the route for an interception. (Ball position and defender leverage are not pose-measurable.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Displacement of Pelvis Center after the plant, resolved along the stem heading in the image plane - it must travel BACK toward the line of scrimmage. Near-zero displacement (standing still) is the fault signal. Plus the shoulder line squaring fully to the quarterback, and horizontal distance of both wrists from Sternum increasing at the catch point (hands extended away from the frame). NOTE: resolved in the image plane, not via MediaPipe Z. Whether the receiver shortened the throw or shielded a defender needs the ball and defender in frame.
records.coaching_cue: Come back to the ball - never wait on it.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Curl - Power Plant
records.ideal_execution_standard: As the eyes find the quarterback, drive the cutting foot down into a tight, compact step directly under the hips. The toe is pulled up sharply into dorsiflexion right before contact, striking with a rigid foot to lock the brakes instantly. Pivot and direct the toe back down the stem toward the line of scrimmage, holding the illusion of a forward sprint until the exact moment of the cut.
records.fault_trigger: THE LUNGING TOE PLANT - reaching too far forward with the planting step and letting the toe point downward before contact. This strips core stability, causes a slide, and tips off the defender early because the running stride visibly changes before the cut.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] THREE signals at the plant frame, on the OUTSIDE foot. (1) COMPACTNESS: horizontal distance between the plant ankle and Pelvis Center - the foot must land directly under the hips, not out in front of the chest frame. (2) DORSIFLEXION: angle between the Foot-Index-to-Heel vector and the Ankle-to-Knee shin vector, with the Heel reaching its lowest vertical position BEFORE the Foot Index at touchdown. A toe-first, downward-pointing strike is the fault signal. (3) TOE DIRECTION: Heel-to-Foot-Index vector pointing directly back down the stem line - a full 180 degree reversal toward the line of scrimmage.
records.coaching_cue: Toe up, under your hips - point it back at the line.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Curl - Stem & Load
records.ideal_execution_standard: Explode off the ball and sprint at full vertical velocity to roughly 12 yards, holding a low pad level and natural full strides to drive the defender into a deep backpedal. At break depth, violently sink the hips and chop the cleats rapidly into the turf - the sudden lowering of the centre of gravity is the braking system that halts the momentum the longer stem has built.
records.fault_trigger: TELEGRAPHING THE STOP - slowing down or rising out of the low pad level a couple of yards before the break point, which lets the defender instantly close the cushion. STIFF-LEGGED BRAKING - trying to stop without sinking the hips, causing a stumble, extra recovery steps, and dangerous stress on the knees.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Forward velocity of Pelvis Center held at top speed with a low shoulder-midpoint height through the stem, then a violent vertical drop of Pelvis Center at the break, expressed in torso lengths. The deeper stem builds more momentum than the Hitch, so expect a 3-step breakdown. Cross-check bilateral knee flexion: hips staying high while the knees absorb the braking force is the stiff-leg fault. Fault signals in the stem: velocity dropping or shoulder height RISING before the break depth. Break depth roughly 12 yards. NOTE: absolute depth needs a scale reference. Depth is the ONLY thing distinguishing the Curl from the Hitch (roughly 5 yards) - the kinematics are identical. Detailed mechanics are held in Cuts - Stop.
records.coaching_cue: Push him deep, then sink your butt - don't rise up early.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Curl - Visual Snap
records.ideal_execution_standard: The millisecond forward momentum halts, snap the head and eyes back around over the inside shoulder to face the quarterback first. Turning the vision inside opens the upper torso and picks up the ball's trajectory before the lower body has finished its pivot.
records.fault_trigger: Head coming round late or after the body has pivoted, so the receiver finishes the break without having found the quarterback - and a ball already in the air arrives before he is looking for it. (Gaze and ball location are not pose-measurable.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Total angular change and peak velocity of head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) rotating back over the inside shoulder toward the quarterback - approaching a 180 degree reversal. Critically, the FRAME at which the rotation begins compared against the frame forward velocity reaches zero, and against the plant contact - the head must lead both. NOTE: orientation only - locating the quarterback and the ball is not confirmable from pose.
records.coaching_cue: The instant you stop - find the quarterback.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Dig - Finish
records.ideal_execution_standard: Drive powerfully off the inside instep of the directing foot, snap the hips wide open, and punch the outside arm across the body to accelerate flat across the field, holding a low, aggressive acceleration posture.
records.fault_trigger: RUNNING FLAT / BANANING - letting the route drift downfield toward the defensive backfield instead of holding a flat, razor-sharp 90-degree line across the middle.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Angle of the Pelvis Center exit trajectory relative to the stem heading - target is a flat 90 degrees, aligned immediately after the plant rather than settling over several strides. The fault signal is any component of that trajectory continuing DOWNFIELD rather than staying flat across. Plus horizontal displacement of the outside wrist across the Sternum midline, confirming the cross-body punch. NOTE: resolved in the image plane against the stem heading.
records.coaching_cue: Flat across - don't drift downfield.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Dig - Power Plant
records.ideal_execution_standard: The instant the eyes locate the inside lane, drive the outside cutting foot down into a compact step tightly aligned within the frame. The toe is pulled upward into dorsiflexion right before contact to establish a firm ankle lock. The cleat slams down directly beneath the hips, instantly pointing the toe at a sharp 90-degree angle toward the middle of the field.
records.fault_trigger: THE FLOPPY-FOOT SLIDE - planting with a loose, downward-pointing toe far out in front of the chest. This lacks the rigidity required to anchor a 90-degree turn, so the shoe slides over the grass and the defender closes the gap. Also: overstriding the break, which elongates the frame, telegraphs the timing, and locks up the hips.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] THREE signals at the plant frame. (1) COMPACTNESS: horizontal distance between the plant ankle and Pelvis Center - should be minimal, the cleat landing directly beneath the hips. A high separation is the fault. (2) DORSIFLEXION: angle between the Foot-Index-to-Heel vector and the Ankle-to-Knee shin vector - toe pulled UP into a rigid ankle lock, heel reaching its lowest vertical point before the Foot Index. (3) TOE DIRECTION: Heel-to-Foot-Index vector pivoting to a sharp 90 degrees toward the middle of the field relative to the stem heading.
records.coaching_cue: Ankle locked, cleat under your hips - don't reach.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Dig - Stem & Load
records.ideal_execution_standard: Run an ultra-aggressive vertical stem for 12-15 yards, pushing directly at the defender's midsection to freeze their leverage and force a deep backpedal respecting the post or go. At break depth, violently drop the weight into the hips and chop the cleats heavily through a 3-step breakdown to absorb the extra momentum the longer stem has built.
records.fault_trigger: BANANA STEMMING - curving the path inward before making the actual break. A rounded line lets an inside-shade defender stay in front of the receiver the whole way. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference and the declared route.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Linear displacement of Pelvis Center and the ankle path along the stem heading, resolved in the image plane - the fault signal is lateral drift (rounding) accumulating BEFORE the break depth is reached. Break depth target 12-15 yards, requiring a 3-step breakdown rather than the In's 2. NOTE: absolute depth needs a scale reference (player height) and the route to be declared; without them, report the measured depth without judging it. Depth is the ONLY thing distinguishing the Dig from the In (10-12 yards) - the kinematics are identical. NOTE: resolved in the image plane, not via MediaPipe Z.
records.coaching_cue: Run it straight and deep - no banana.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Dig - Visual Snap
records.ideal_execution_standard: At the absolute peak of the breakdown, snap the head and eyes around to face the quarterback first. The visual snap opens the torso and clears vision to read the inside linebackers before the body commits.
records.fault_trigger: Head turning with or after the plant rather than leading it, so the receiver breaks into the middle without having cleared his vision for crashing inside defenders. (Gaze and defender positions are not pose-measurable.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak angular velocity of head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) rotating toward the middle of the field, and the FRAME at which that rotation begins compared against the plant foot's ground-contact frame - the head must lead. Plus shoulder-line rotation following the head. NOTE: orientation only - whether the receiver actually READ the inside linebackers is not confirmable from pose.
records.coaching_cue: Snap the eyes inside - see the window before you turn.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Flat - Angle Plant
records.ideal_execution_standard: The instant the eyes find the sideline, drive the INSIDE foot down into a sharp, compact step positioned firmly beneath the body weight. The toe is pulled up into dorsiflexion before the foot strikes to ground cleanly. Instantly point the toe and direct the final step down a flat 90-degree track toward the boundary, masking the horizontal break until the last possible instant.
records.fault_trigger: THE FLOPPY-FOOT SLIDE - planting with a loose, downward-pointing toe far out in front of the chest. This lacks the rigidity required to anchor a 90-degree turn, so the shoe slides over the grass and the defender closes the gap.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] THREE signals at the plant frame, on the INSIDE foot (mirroring the Cross, which plants outside). (1) COMPACTNESS: horizontal position of the plant ankle relative to Pelvis Center - the cleat must land firmly beneath the body weight, not out in front of the chest. (2) DORSIFLEXION: angle between the Foot-Index-to-Heel vector and the Ankle-to-Knee shin vector - the toe pulled up before the foot strikes, grounding the receiver cleanly. A loose, downward-pointing toe is the fault signal. (3) TOE DIRECTION: Heel-to-Foot-Index vector pivoting to a flat 90 degrees outward toward the boundary relative to the release heading.
records.coaching_cue: Toe up, under yourself - point it at the sideline.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Flat - Finish
records.ideal_execution_standard: Push violently off the inside instep of the directing foot, sprint flat along the line toward the boundary, snap the eyes back over the inside shoulder to look for the ball, and secure the catch while bracing to turn upfield.
records.fault_trigger: DRIFTING DOWNHILL - allowing the route to angle backward toward the line of scrimmage. The line must stay flat and parallel to the line of scrimmage to maximise the open void. (Ball location needs ball tracking.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Angle of the Pelvis Center exit trajectory relative to the release heading - target is a flat 90 degrees held linear toward the sideline. The fault signal is any component of that trajectory travelling BACK toward the line of scrimmage. Plus head yaw snapping back over the inside shoulder after the break, and horizontal displacement of the outside wrist confirming the arm drive. NOTE: resolved in the image plane; ball location needs ball tracking.
records.coaching_cue: Flat to the boundary - don't drift back.

records.ideal_execution_standard: Explode vertically off the line for 2 to 3 hard steps, driving the pads forward to threaten the defender's leverage and make them respect a vertical release. Then prepare to redirect sideways by subtly sinking the hips, keeping the feet moving at full speed with no choppy or gathering steps.
