The fault signal is lateral drift toward the sideline beginning immediately off the line rather than after the vertical steps. Plus a subtle vertical drop of Pelvis Center WITHOUT any reduction in stride length or step frequency - a speed-cut load, not a breakdown. Break depth 1-3 yards. NOTE: absolute depth needs a scale reference; the step COUNT does not, and is the more reliable signal here. Detailed mechanics are held in Cuts - Speed.
records.coaching_cue: Two hard steps vertical first - don't fade to the sideline.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Flat - Visual Snap
records.ideal_execution_standard: At break depth, snap the head and eyes sharply toward the sideline first. The visual focus locks onto the boundary line, which naturally uncoils the neck and shoulders into the flat lane.
records.fault_trigger: Head turning with the plant or after it rather than leading it, so the shoulders never uncoil into the lane and the break is slower than a quick-game route can afford. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak angular velocity of head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) rotating toward the boundary, and the FRAME at which that rotation begins compared against the plant foot's ground-contact frame - the head must lead. Plus shoulder-line rotation following the head (the neck and shoulders uncoiling into the flat lane). NOTE: orientation only - actual EYE GAZE is not measurable, and the boundary line is not reliably in frame in a solo clip.
records.coaching_cue: Eyes to the boundary first - let the shoulders follow.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Go - Finish
records.ideal_execution_standard: Keep the hands down and running until the absolute last moment so the defender is not tipped off to the ball's arrival, then shoot the arms out late, secure the catch away from the frame, and protect the ball.
records.fault_trigger: EARLY HANDS - running with the hands extended upward for several yards waiting for the ball. This is a clear signal to the defender, letting them play the arms and break up the pass. (Ball arrival timing needs ball tracking.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Vertical height of both wrists relative to Sternum held at normal sprint-pump level across the whole route, with elevation occurring only in the final frames before the catch. The measurement is the FRAME at which the wrists rise above sprint level - any sustained elevation earlier is the fault signal. Plus head yaw turning to track over the shoulder while the Pelvis Center path stays linear. NOTE: the ball is NOT trackable without object detection, so the app can see WHEN the hands went up but not whether that timing matched the ball's arrival.
records.coaching_cue: Hands down until the last second - then shoot them.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Go - Release
records.ideal_execution_standard: Explode off the ball with a violent, low pad-level release to clear the press defender's hands and establish the vertical track, then transition from acceleration into full top-speed sprint posture - stride lengths opening to maximum expansion with the chin tucked.
records.fault_trigger: Standing up out of the release rather than driving low, or strides failing to expand into top-end sprint mechanics - either way the receiver never reaches the speed the route depends on.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Stride length per step along the release heading, expressed in shoulder widths, EXPANDING progressively from the high-frequency release steps to maximum extension at top speed. Plus peak vertical knee height relative to Pelvis Center, and the rate of rise of the shoulder midpoint out of the low release posture. NOTE: resolved in the image plane against the release heading. There is NO break in this route - the whole stem is the technique.
records.coaching_cue: Low out of the gate, then open your stride up.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Go - Stack
records.ideal_execution_standard: Running neck-and-neck with the defender, use a high-speed hand swipe or arm bar to clear their trailing reach, working to stack the body directly in front of their path and strip away their recovery angle - while the head stays locked downfield.
records.fault_trigger: LOOKING BACK EARLY - turning the head to look for the ball while it is still in the air and outside the catch radius. Looking back early kills top-end speed and tells the defender to play the hands. (Defender position and stack are not pose-measurable.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak velocity of the near wrist and elbow on a lateral or upward clearing path away from the sprint pump cycle, indicating a swipe or arm bar. Plus, critically, head yaw held at zero relative to the release heading - the FRAME of any premature rotation toward the quarterback is the fault signal. NOTE: the defender is NOT in frame in a solo clip, so whether the receiver actually stacked them or cleared their hands cannot be confirmed - only that the arm action occurred and the head stayed forward.
records.coaching_cue: Clear his hands, stack him - don't peek.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Go - Vertical Run
records.ideal_execution_standard: The running stride stays completely natural and uninterrupted, steps landing compact and directly beneath the centre of mass without overstriding. The toes pull up into sharp dorsiflexion on every stride to hold a rigid, explosive ankle lock against the turf while the eyes track the ball over the shoulder.
records.fault_trigger: OVERSTRIDING / FLOPPY FOOTWORK - reaching too far forward to try to run faster, or running with a loose, downward-pointing toe. This strips core stability, caps top-end speed, and costs balance down the sideline.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Applied to EVERY stride rather than a single plant, unlike the cut techniques. (1) DORSIFLEXION: angle between the Foot-Index-to-Heel vector and the Ankle-to-Knee shin vector at each ground contact - the toe pulled up into a rigid ankle lock. A Foot Index pointing downward at impact is the fault signal. (2) COMPACTNESS: horizontal position of the landing ankle relative to Pelvis Center at each strike - landing beneath the centre of mass, not reaching ahead. (3) LINEARITY: lateral deviation of the ankle path and Pelvis Center from the release heading, which should stay near zero.
records.coaching_cue: Toes up every step - don't reach for speed.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Hitch - Finish
records.ideal_execution_standard: Drive powerfully off the inside instep of the directing foot, open the chest completely to the quarterback, work back downhill toward the ball to shorten the distance of the throw, and secure the catch with the hands extended away from the frame.
records.fault_trigger: WAITING ON THE BALL - standing still after making the cut. The receiver must actively run back downhill toward the ball to stop a trailing defender undercutting the route for an interception. (Ball position and defender leverage are not pose-measurable.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Displacement of Pelvis Center after the plant, resolved along the stem heading in the image plane - it must travel BACK toward the line of scrimmage. Near-zero displacement (standing still) is the fault signal. Plus the shoulder line squaring fully to the quarterback, and horizontal distance of both wrists from Sternum increasing at the catch point (hands extended away from the frame). NOTE: resolved in the image plane, not via MediaPipe Z. Whether the receiver shortened the throw or shielded a defender needs the ball and defender in frame.
records.coaching_cue: Come back to the ball - never wait on it.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Hitch - Power Plant
records.ideal_execution_standard: As the eyes find the quarterback, drive the cutting foot down into a tight, compact step directly under the hips. The toe is pulled up sharply into dorsiflexion right before contact, striking with a rigid foot to lock the brakes instantly. Pivot and direct the toe back down the stem toward the line of scrimmage, holding the illusion of a forward sprint until the exact moment of the cut.
records.fault_trigger: THE LUNGING TOE PLANT - reaching too far forward with the planting step and letting the toe point downward before contact. This strips core stability, causes a slide, and tips off the defender early because the running stride visibly changes before the cut.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] THREE signals at the plant frame, on the OUTSIDE foot. (1) COMPACTNESS: horizontal distance between the plant ankle and Pelvis Center - the foot must land directly under the hips, not out in front of the chest frame. (2) DORSIFLEXION: angle between the Foot-Index-to-Heel vector and the Ankle-to-Knee shin vector, with the Heel reaching its lowest vertical position BEFORE the Foot Index at touchdown. A toe-first, downward-pointing strike is the fault signal. (3) TOE DIRECTION: Heel-to-Foot-Index vector pointing directly back down the stem line - a full 180 degree reversal toward the line of scrimmage.
records.coaching_cue: Toe up, under your hips - point it back at the line.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Hitch - Stem & Load
records.ideal_execution_standard: Explode off the ball and sprint at full vertical velocity to roughly 5 yards, holding a low pad level and natural full strides to force the defender into a deep backpedal. At break depth, violently sink the hips and chop the cleats rapidly into the turf - the sudden lowering of the centre of gravity is the braking system that halts forward momentum.
records.fault_trigger: TELEGRAPHING THE STOP - slowing down or rising out of the low pad level a couple of yards before the break point, which lets the defender instantly close the cushion. STIFF-LEGGED BRAKING - trying to stop without sinking the hips, causing a stumble, extra recovery steps, and dangerous stress on the knees.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Forward velocity of Pelvis Center held at top speed with a low shoulder-midpoint height through the stem, then a violent vertical drop of Pelvis Center at the break, expressed in torso lengths. Cross-check bilateral knee flexion: hips staying high while the knees absorb the braking force is the stiff-leg fault. Fault signals in the stem: velocity dropping or shoulder height RISING before the break depth. Break depth roughly 5 yards. NOTE: absolute depth needs a scale reference; without it, report the measured depth without judging it. Detailed mechanics are held in Cuts - Stop.
records.coaching_cue: Sell the go, then sink your butt - don't rise up early.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Hitch - Visual Snap
records.ideal_execution_standard: The millisecond forward momentum halts, snap the head and eyes back around over the inside shoulder to face the quarterback first. Turning the vision inside opens the upper torso and picks up the ball's trajectory before the lower body has finished its pivot.
records.fault_trigger: Head coming round late or after the body has pivoted, so the receiver finishes the break without having found the quarterback - and on a route this quick the ball is usually already out. (Gaze and ball location are not pose-measurable.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Total angular change and peak velocity of head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) rotating back over the inside shoulder toward the quarterback - approaching a 180 degree reversal. Critically, the FRAME at which the rotation begins compared against the frame forward velocity reaches zero, and against the plant contact - the head must lead both. NOTE: orientation only - locating the quarterback and the ball is not confirmable from pose.
records.coaching_cue: The instant you stop - find the quarterback.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - In - Finish
records.ideal_execution_standard: Drive powerfully off the inside instep of the directing foot, snap the hips wide open, and punch the outside arm across the body to accelerate flat across the field, holding a low, aggressive acceleration posture.
records.fault_trigger: RUNNING FLAT / BANANING - letting the route drift downfield toward the defensive backfield instead of holding a flat, razor-sharp 90-degree line across the middle.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Angle of the Pelvis Center exit trajectory relative to the stem heading - target is a flat 90 degrees, aligned immediately after the plant rather than settling over several strides. The fault signal is any component of that trajectory continuing DOWNFIELD rather than staying flat across. Plus horizontal displacement of the outside wrist across the Sternum midline, confirming the cross-body punch. NOTE: resolved in the image plane against the stem heading.
records.coaching_cue: Flat across - don't drift downfield.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - In - Power Plant
records.ideal_execution_standard: The instant the eyes locate the inside lane, drive the outside cutting foot down into a compact step tightly aligned within the frame. The toe is pulled upward into dorsiflexion right before contact to establish a firm ankle lock. The cleat slams down directly beneath the hips, instantly pointing the toe at a sharp 90-degree angle toward the middle of the field.
records.fault_trigger: OVERSTRIDING THE BREAK - reaching too far inside with a long, diving step. This elongates the body frame, tells the defender exactly when the break is coming, and locks up the hips so the receiver cannot accelerate smoothly out of the cut. Also: THE FLOPPY-FOOT SLIDE - planting with a loose, downward-pointing toe out in front of the chest, lacking the rigidity to anchor a 90-degree turn, so the shoe slides over the grass.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] THREE signals at the plant frame. (1) COMPACTNESS: horizontal distance between the plant ankle and Pelvis Center - should be minimal, the cleat landing directly beneath the hips. A high separation is the overstriding fault. (2) DORSIFLEXION: angle between the Foot-Index-to-Heel vector and the Ankle-to-Knee shin vector - toe pulled UP into a rigid ankle lock, heel reaching its lowest vertical point before the Foot Index. (3) TOE DIRECTION: Heel-to-Foot-Index vector pivoting to a sharp 90 degrees toward the middle of the field relative to the stem heading.
records.coaching_cue: Ankle locked, cleat under your hips - don't reach.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - In - Stem & Load
records.ideal_execution_standard: Sprint hard downfield on a strictly straight line for 10-12 yards, pushing the vertical stem through the defender's outside shoulder to force them to protect the deep outside lane. Two steps before break depth, drop the weight violently into the hips and chop the cleats to counteract forward momentum.
records.fault_trigger: BANANA STEMMING - curving the path inward before making the actual break. A rounded line lets an inside-shade defender stay in front of the receiver the whole way. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference and the declared route.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Linear displacement of Pelvis Center and the ankle path along the stem heading, resolved in the image plane - the fault signal is lateral drift (rounding) accumulating BEFORE the break depth is reached. Break depth target 10-12 yards. NOTE: absolute depth needs a scale reference (player height) and the route to be declared; without them, report the measured depth without judging it. Depth is the ONLY thing distinguishing the In from the Dig (12-15 yards) - the kinematics are identical. NOTE: resolved in the image plane, not via MediaPipe Z.
records.coaching_cue: Run it straight - no banana.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - In - Visual Snap
records.ideal_execution_standard: At the absolute peak of deceleration, snap the head and eyes around to face the middle of the field first. The visual snap opens the torso and clears vision to read the inside linebackers before the body commits.
records.fault_trigger: Head turning with or after the plant rather than leading it, so the receiver breaks into the middle without having cleared his vision for crashing inside defenders. (Gaze and defender positions are not pose-measurable.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak angular velocity of head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) rotating toward the middle of the field, and the FRAME at which that rotation begins compared against the plant foot's ground-contact frame - the head must lead. Plus shoulder-line rotation following the head. NOTE: orientation only - whether the receiver actually READ the inside linebackers is not confirmable from pose.
records.coaching_cue: Snap the eyes inside - see the window before you turn.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Out - Finish
records.ideal_execution_standard: Push violently off the inside instep of the directing foot, flip the hips wide open, and punch the outside arm across the body to accelerate flat along the 90-degree line toward the sideline.
records.fault_trigger: DRIFTING DOWNHILL - allowing the route to angle backward toward the line of scrimmage. The line must stay flat and parallel to the line of scrimmage to keep outrunning the trailing defender.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Angle of the Pelvis Center exit trajectory relative to the stem heading - target is a flat 90 degrees, held linear. The fault signal is any component of that trajectory travelling BACK toward the original line of scrimmage. Plus horizontal displacement of the outside wrist across the Sternum midline at the drive-out, confirming the cross-body arm punch. NOTE: resolved in the image plane against the stem heading, not via MediaPipe Z.
records.coaching_cue: Punch across and run flat - never drift back.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Out - Power Plant
records.ideal_execution_standard: As the eyes find the boundary, slam the inside foot down into a tight, compact step directly under the centre of mass. The toe is pulled up sharply into dorsiflexion right before contact, striking with a rigid foot to lock the brakes. Instantly pivot and point the toe down a flat 90-degree track toward the sideline, masking the break until the last possible instant.
records.fault_trigger: THE LUNGING SLIDE - lunging too far forward with a loose, downward-pointing toe. The over-extension lacks the rigidity to anchor a 90-degree turn, so the shoe slides over the grass and the defender closes the gap.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] THREE signals at the plant frame. (1) COMPACTNESS: horizontal position of the plant ankle relative to Pelvis Center - the foot must land strictly under the centre of mass, not ahead of it. Also check the ankle is not ahead of the knee. (2) DORSIFLEXION: angle between the Foot-Index-to-Heel vector and the Ankle-to-Knee shin vector - the toe pulled UP pre-impact, with the heel reaching its lowest vertical point before the Foot Index at touchdown. (3) TOE DIRECTION: Heel-to-Foot-Index vector pivoting to a flat 90 degrees toward the sideline relative to the stem heading.
records.coaching_cue: Toe up, plant under yourself, point it at the sideline.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Out - Stem & Load
records.ideal_execution_standard: Drive off the line at full velocity for 10-12 yards with pads leaning forward and natural full strides, forcing the defender into an aggressive backpedal for fear of the go route. Two steps before break depth, violently sink the hips and chop the cleats to control speed - without standing up or slowing the arm pump.
records.fault_trigger: THE DEAD GIVEAWAY - slowing the arm pump or raising the chest before reaching break depth, alerting the defender to clamp down on the out route. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference and the declared route.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Vertical drop of Pelvis Center beginning roughly 2 steps before the break, expressed in torso lengths. Break depth target 10-12 yards - NOTE: absolute depth needs a scale reference (player height) and the route to be declared; without them, report the measured depth without judging it. Fault signals: wrist displacement amplitude decreasing, or Sternum vertical height RISING, at any point before the break depth is reached. Detailed breakdown mechanics are held in Cuts - Stop.
records.coaching_cue: Sell the go - keep pumping, drop your weight late.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Out - Visual Snap
records.ideal_execution_standard: At the exact peak of deceleration, snap the head and eyes sharply toward the sideline first. The visual turn shifts equilibrium and opens the upper torso toward the boundary before the feet leave the turf.
records.fault_trigger: Head turning at the same time as the plant or after it, so the body commits before the eyes have opened the boundary - the torso does not pre-rotate and the break is slower. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak angular velocity of head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) toward the sideline, and critically the FRAME at which that rotation begins compared against the plant foot's ground-contact frame - the head must lead the plant. NOTE: orientation only - actual EYE GAZE is not measurable from the 33-point pose model.
records.coaching_cue: Eyes to the boundary first - then the foot.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Post - Angle Plant
records.ideal_execution_standard: The millisecond the eyes locate the post, drive the OUTSIDE cutting foot down into a compact step tightly aligned within the frame. The toe is pulled upward into dorsiflexion right before contact to establish a firm ankle lock. The cleat slams down directly beneath the hips, instantly pointing the toe at a sharp 45-degree angle toward the post.
records.fault_trigger: OVERSTRIDING THE BREAK - reaching too far inside with a long, diving step. This elongates the body frame, tells the defender exactly when the break is coming, and locks up the hips so the receiver cannot accelerate smoothly out of the cut.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] THREE signals at the plant frame, on the OUTSIDE foot (mirroring the Corner, which plants inside). (1) COMPACTNESS: displacement between the plant ankle and Pelvis Center along the stem heading - the cleat must land directly beneath the hips, not reaching ahead. High separation is the overstriding fault. (2) DORSIFLEXION: angle between the Foot-Index-to-Heel vector and the Ankle-to-Knee shin vector - toe pulled UP into a rigid ankle lock, heel reaching its lowest vertical point before the Foot Index. (3) TOE DIRECTION: Heel-to-Foot-Index vector pivoting to 45 degrees INWARD toward the post relative to the stem heading.
records.coaching_cue: Ankle locked, cleat under your hips - point it at the post.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Post - Finish
records.ideal_execution_standard: Drive powerfully off the inside instep of the directing foot, snap the hips wide open, and punch the outside arm across the body to accelerate down the 45-degree track, holding a low, aggressive acceleration posture.
records.fault_trigger: FLATTENING THE ROUTE - letting the route drift flat toward the opposite sideline instead of holding a true 45-degree angle toward the goal post, which takes the receiver out of the intended throwing window.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Angle of the Pelvis Center exit trajectory relative to the stem heading - target is a strict 45 degrees toward the post, held linear. The fault signal is that angle opening toward 90 degrees (flattening across toward the opposite sideline). Plus horizontal displacement of the outside wrist across the Sternum midline, confirming the cross-body punch. NOTE: resolved in the image plane against the stem heading.
records.coaching_cue: Hold 45 at the post - don't flatten across.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Post - Stem & Load
records.ideal_execution_standard: Sprint hard downfield for 10-12 yards (12-15 on the deeper variation), pushing the vertical stem straight through the defender's outside shoulder to force them to protect the deep outside lane. One step before the break, drop the weight subtly into the hips and prepare to transfer laterally - without any choppy or gathering steps.
records.fault_trigger: BANANA STEMMING - curving the path inward before making the actual break. A rounded line lets an inside-shade defender stay in front of the receiver the whole way. Also: chopping or gathering into the load, which turns a speed cut into a visible breakdown. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference and the called depth.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Linear displacement of Pelvis Center and the ankle path along the stem heading, resolved in the image plane - the fault signal is lateral drift toward the middle accumulating BEFORE the break point. Plus a subtle vertical drop of Pelvis Center (roughly an inch on an adult frame) one step before the break, WITHOUT any reduction in stride length or step frequency - this is a speed-cut load, not a breakdown. Break depth 10-12 yards standard; a deeper variation runs 12-15. NOTE: absolute depth needs a scale reference (player height) and the called depth; without them, report the measured depth without judging it. Detailed mechanics are held in Cuts - Speed.
records.coaching_cue: Straight through his outside shoulder - no banana.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Post - Visual Snap
records.ideal_execution_standard: At the peak of the stem, snap the head and eyes around to face the near goal post first. The visual snap opens the torso and clears vision to read the safety rotation before the body commits.
records.fault_trigger: Head turning with the plant or after it rather than leading it, so the receiver breaks inside without having read the safety rotation and the torso never pre-rotates. (Gaze and safety position are not pose-measurable.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak angular velocity of head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) toward the near goal post, and critically the FRAME at which that rotation begins compared against the plant foot's ground-contact frame - the head must lead the plant. NOTE: orientation only - actual EYE GAZE is not measurable, and whether the receiver READ the safety rotation cannot be confirmed from a solo clip.
records.coaching_cue: Eyes to the post first - read the safety.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Seam - Finish
records.ideal_execution_standard: Expect a heavy hit from a closing safety or linebacker over the middle. Keep the hands down late to mask the ball's arrival, then shoot the arms up violently to snap the ball out of the air at its highest point, instantly tucking it to protect against incoming contact.
records.fault_trigger: EXPOSING THE BALL - catching with the body loose or waiting for the ball to hit the chest. Over the middle, failing to snatch with extended hands and instantly tuck results in drops and forced fumbles. (Ball position and contact are not pose-measurable.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Vertical height of both wrists relative to Sternum held at sprint-pump level, then a RAPID elevation above the shoulder line at the catch point, immediately followed by the wrists collapsing back toward Sternum (the tuck). The measurement is the speed of the rise and the immediacy of the tuck. Fault signals: wrists staying low at the catch point, or no tuck following the catch. Plus shoulder line squaring at the catch to brace for contact. NOTE: the ball is NOT trackable without object detection, so the app can see the arm action and tuck but not whether the ball was caught at its apex.
records.coaching_cue: Snatch it high, tuck it now - the hit is coming.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Seam - Release
records.ideal_execution_standard: Explode off the ball with a violent, low pad-level release to clear the press defender's hands and establish a strict linear track down the hashes or the seam lane, then transition smoothly into top-end sprint posture with stride lengths opening to maximum expansion, chin tucked and core locked on the track.
records.fault_trigger: BAILING OFF-TRACK - drifting wide toward the sideline or inside toward the middle right off the snap. Scurrying off the track ruins the spacing of the concept and runs the receiver straight into zone defenders.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Stride length per step along the release heading, expressed in shoulder widths, EXPANDING progressively from the high-frequency release steps to maximum extension at top speed. Plus lateral deviation of the ankle path and Pelvis Center from the release heading, which must stay near zero - the seam lane is narrow and drift ruins the concept spacing. Also the rate of rise of the shoulder midpoint out of the low release posture. NOTE: resolved in the image plane against the release heading. There is NO break in this route.
records.coaching_cue: Low out, then stretch it - stay on your track.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Seam - Squeeze
records.ideal_execution_standard: Pushing through the intermediate zone at 10-12 yards, expect a collision or squeeze from interior linebackers or safeties. Use a high-speed hand swipe, chop or arm bar to clear their contact while holding the vertical line without drifting off-track or losing a step.
records.fault_trigger: SLOWING DOWN FOR CONTACT - decelerating or stutter-stepping when an inside linebacker tries to reroute or jam. The receiver must sprint through the contact and use the hands to clear without dropping speed. (Defender contact is not pose-measurable.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak velocity of the wrists and elbows on a lateral or upward clearing path away from the sprint pump cycle, indicating a swipe, chop or arm bar. Critically, cross-check forward velocity of Pelvis Center across the same frames - it must NOT drop. Any deceleration or stutter-step coinciding with the arm action is the fault signal. NOTE: the defender is NOT in frame in a solo clip, so whether contact was actually cleared cannot be confirmed - only that the arm action occurred and speed was held.
records.coaching_cue: Run through the contact - hands clear it, feet don't stop.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Seam - Vertical Run
records.ideal_execution_standard: Squeeze tightly into the defensive void with the running track completely straight. Steps stay compact and directly beneath the centre of mass without overstriding, toes pulling up into sharp dorsiflexion on every stride for a rigid ankle lock, while the eyes track the ball over the inside shoulder.
records.fault_trigger: OVERSTRIDING / FLOPPY FOOTWORK - reaching too far forward to try to outrun a deep safety, or running with a loose, downward-pointing toe. This strips core stability and caps top-end speed. Also: drifting laterally out of the void.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Applied to EVERY stride rather than a single plant. (1) DORSIFLEXION: angle between the Foot-Index-to-Heel vector and the Ankle-to-Knee shin vector at each ground contact - the toe pulled up into a rigid ankle lock. A Foot Index pointing downward at impact is the fault signal. (2) COMPACTNESS: horizontal position of the landing ankle relative to Pelvis Center at each strike - landing beneath the centre of mass, not extending beyond it. (3) LINEARITY: lateral deviation of the ankle path and Pelvis Center from the release heading, held near zero to stay in the void. (4) Head yaw rotating to track over the INSIDE shoulder while the Pelvis Center path stays linear.
records.coaching_cue: Toes up, straight down the lane - look over the inside shoulder.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Slant - Angle Plant
records.ideal_execution_standard: The split-second the eyes turn, drive the outside foot down into a controlled step tightly aligned within the frame. The toe is pulled up into dorsiflexion before impact to establish a firm ankle lock, and the step is not overextended. The cleat slams down directly beneath the hips, instantly directing the toe at a sharp 45 degrees toward the middle to slice across the defender's face without losing linear body control.
records.fault_trigger: OVERSTRIDING THE BREAK - reaching too far inside with a long, diving step. This elongates the body frame, tells the defender exactly when the break is coming, and locks up the hips so the receiver cannot accelerate smoothly out of the cut.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] THREE signals at the plant frame, on the OUTSIDE foot. (1) COMPACTNESS: displacement between the plant ankle and Pelvis Center - the cleat must land directly beneath the hips, not overextended. High separation is the overstriding fault. (2) DORSIFLEXION: angle between the Foot-Index-to-Heel vector and the Ankle-to-Knee shin vector - toe pulled UP into a firm ankle lock before impact. (3) TOE DIRECTION: Heel-to-Foot-Index vector directing to a sharp 45 degrees inward relative to the release heading.
records.coaching_cue: Toe up, under your hips - slice across his face.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Slant - Finish
records.ideal_execution_standard: Roll the body weight smoothly off the directing foot, punch the outside arm violently across the body to hold top sprinting speed, maintain the 45-degree trajectory, and catch the ball cleanly in stride.
records.fault_trigger: RUNNING FLAT - flattening the route out horizontally toward the opposite sideline. The receiver must hold a strict 45-degree angle to keep outrunning the trailing defender. (Ball location needs ball tracking.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Angle of the Pelvis Center exit trajectory relative to the release heading - target is a strict 45 degrees held linear. The fault signal is that angle opening toward 90 degrees (flattening across). Plus horizontal displacement of the outside wrist across the Sternum midline confirming the cross-body punch, and forward velocity sustained through the break rather than dropping. NOTE: resolved in the image plane; catching the ball in stride needs ball tracking.
records.coaching_cue: Hold 45 and roll through it - don't flatten.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Slant - Stem & Load
records.ideal_execution_standard: Fire off the line hard for 3 direct vertical strides in a fierce sprint-sell posture - the path must look identical to a go route to freeze the defender's feet and leverage. On the second step, subtly drop the hips an inch into a compact athletic posture while the feet keep moving at full velocity.
records.fault_trigger: BANANA STEMMING - curving the path inward before the actual break, letting an inside-shade defender stay in front the whole way. CHOPPING FEET - gathering or stutter-stepping before the break; a slant relies entirely on pure unmitigated speed, and chopping ruins the separation.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Count and linearity of the vertical strides before the break - target 3 direct strides with lateral deviation from the release heading near zero. Plus a subtle vertical drop of Pelvis Center on the second step, WITHOUT any reduction in stride length or increase in step frequency. Break at 3 steps / roughly 5 yards. NOTE: absolute depth needs a scale reference; the step COUNT does not, and is the more reliable signal here. Detailed mechanics are held in Cuts - Speed.
records.coaching_cue: Three hard steps straight - no chop, no banana.

records.name: WR - Routes - Tree - Slant - Visual Snap
records.ideal_execution_standard: At the exact peak of the third stride, snap the head and eyes inside across the middle of the field first. The visual snap instantly clears vision to read the inside linebackers and pick up the ball's release.
records.fault_trigger: Head turning with or after the plant rather than leading it, so the receiver breaks across the defender's face without having cleared his vision - and on a route this quick, the ball is often already out. (Gaze and defender positions are not pose-measurable.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Peak angular velocity of head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) rotating inside across the middle, and critically the FRAME at which that rotation begins compared against the third stride's ground-contact frame - the head must lead the plant. NOTE: orientation only - whether the receiver actually READ the inside linebackers or picked up the release cannot be confirmed from a solo clip.
records.coaching_cue: Eyes inside at the top of step three.

records.name: WR - Standard - Stance - Base Width
records.ideal_execution_standard: Feet are approximately shoulder width apart, providing a stable and explosive base. The stance is wide enough for balance without restricting the first step.
records.fault_trigger: Base too narrow to balance, or so wide it restricts the first step and forces a false step to recover.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Ankle-to-ankle horizontal distance compared against shoulder width (L-R Shoulder) as the scale unit - target approximately 1.0x shoulder width. Size-independent. Measurable from a static frame.
records.coaching_cue: Stable, not stuck — wide enough to balance, narrow enough to go.

records.name: WR - Standard - Stance - Body Angle
records.ideal_execution_standard: Upper body is positioned at approximately the same forward angle as the loaded front shin, creating a connected lower- and upper-body position. Avoid excessive bending at the waist.
records.fault_trigger: Torso angle diverging from the shin angle - typically folding forward at the waist with the chest well ahead of the shin line, or standing the torso upright while the shin stays loaded, disconnecting upper and lower body.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Torso vector (hip midpoint to shoulder midpoint) angle compared against the front shin vector (Ankle to Knee) - the two should be approximately parallel in the loaded stance. Difference between the angles is the measurement. Measurable from a static frame.
records.coaching_cue: Match your chest to your shin - don't fold at the waist.

records.name: WR - Standard - Stance - Foot Alignment
records.ideal_execution_standard: Inside foot is forward, toward the ball. Feet maintain the appropriate stagger and orientation to allow the receiver to release without a false step. The front foot carries a very slight inward turn - enough to aid the release, but not so much that the turn carries up into the hips and opens them inside. The front foot supports the initial roll-off movement.
records.fault_trigger: Outside foot forward instead of the inside foot; stagger too deep or too shallow to release cleanly; front toe square or turned outward rather than slightly in; or the inward turn overdone so it pulls the hips inside and opens them before the snap. (Which foot is 'inside' depends on alignment side - not determinable from a solo clip.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Fore-aft offset between the two ankles (stagger depth, in shoulder-width units); plus FRONT-FOOT TOE ANGLE from the Heel-to-Foot-Index vector, measured relative to the stance facing - a slight inward turn is correct, an excessive one is a fault. Cross-check the hip line (L-R Hip vector) to confirm the turn has NOT carried into the hips. NOTE: which foot should be forward is the INSIDE foot, and 'inside' depends on which side of the formation the receiver is aligned - that side is not determinable from a solo clip and must be supplied or reported without judging.
records.coaching_cue: Inside foot up, toe just cracked in - foot turns, hips don't.

records.name: WR - Standard - Stance - Hand Position
records.ideal_execution_standard: Hands remain relaxed, uncrossed, and independent. Hands are positioned near the waist or slightly higher in front of the chest depending on anticipated coverage. Hands remain free to immediately react to a press defender.
records.fault_trigger: Hands crossed over the body's midline, clamped tight to the torso, or held so low or high that the receiver cannot react to a press. Arms rigid rather than relaxed. (Finger and grip detail needs the Hand landmarker.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Wrist height relative to Sternum and Pelvis Center (waist-to-chest band); horizontal separation between the wrists (uncrossed, independent); elbow angle for relaxed vs rigid. Hand OPENNESS and finger detail need the Hand landmarker - not available from the 33-point pose model.
records.coaching_cue: Hands loose and free - ready to fight hands.

records.name: WR - Standard - Stance - Head / Eyes
records.ideal_execution_standard: Head is turned inside toward the football before the snap, with eyes locked onto the ball. The receiver uses the football's movement as the visual snap cue rather than reacting to the quarterback's verbal cadence. Head position remains controlled and stable so the receiver can explode immediately when the ball is snapped without a false start.
records.fault_trigger: Head facing straight downfield rather than turned inside to the ball, or head unstable/bobbing pre-snap so the receiver reacts late. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only. Ball location needs ball tracking.)
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Head yaw from Nose position relative to the ear midpoint, compared against the shoulder line - confirms the head is turned inside rather than facing straight downfield. Head STABILITY measurable as low variance across pre-snap frames. NOTE: actual EYE GAZE is not measurable from the 33-point pose model - orientation only. Whether the head is oriented at the BALL needs ball tracking; which side is 'inside' needs the alignment side.
records.coaching_cue: Eyes on the ball - go on movement, not sound.

records.name: WR - Standard - Stance - Hip Alignment
records.ideal_execution_standard: Hips remain loaded underneath the torso and prepared to drive toward the release. Hips should not be excessively opened before movement begins.
records.fault_trigger: Hips opened toward the release before movement begins, giving away direction, or hips drifting out from under the torso so the drive is weakened.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Hip-line angle (L-R Hip vector) relative to the shoulder line and the stance facing; plus horizontal position of Pelvis Center relative to the base. Measurable from a static frame.
records.coaching_cue: Hips loaded under you - don't open early.

records.name: WR - Standard - Stance - Knee Flexion
records.ideal_execution_standard: Front knee is bent rather than locked. The knee tracks forward toward the toe while maintaining an athletic loaded position. Rear knee remains flexed enough to contribute to the first movement.
records.fault_trigger: Front knee locked or straight, knee collapsing inside or outside the toe line, or rear knee too extended to contribute to the first movement.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Knee angle from the Hip-Knee-Ankle vectors on both legs; plus horizontal tracking of the front knee over the front Foot Index (knee-over-toe). Measurable from a static frame.
records.coaching_cue: Knee over toe - bent and loaded, never locked.

records.name: WR - Standard - Stance - Pad Level
records.ideal_execution_standard: Chest and hips are lowered into an athletic position. The shoulders/chest are positioned over the front knee, creating forward readiness without excessive crouching.
records.fault_trigger: Standing too tall with no forward readiness, or crouching so low the receiver cannot release cleanly. Chest behind or well past the front knee.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Vertical height of Sternum and the hip midpoint (Pelvis Center) expressed in torso lengths; plus horizontal offset of Sternum over the front knee. Measurable from a static frame.
records.coaching_cue: Chest over the front knee - low, not folded.

records.name: WR - Standard - Stance - Shoulder Alignment
records.ideal_execution_standard: Shoulders remain controlled and aligned with the intended release position. The upper body should not rotate excessively away from the line before movement begins.
records.fault_trigger: Shoulders rotated away from the line before the snap, telegraphing the release direction to the defender, or shoulder line unlevel enough to unbalance the first step.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Shoulder-line angle (L-R Shoulder vector) relative to the hip line and to the stance's facing direction. Measurable from a static frame; whether the rotation matches the INTENDED release direction needs the release itself or a declared route.
records.coaching_cue: Square and quiet - don't tip the release.

records.name: WR - Standard - Stance - Stance Stability / Readiness
records.ideal_execution_standard: Receiver remains stable but immediately movable. The stance is sufficiently loaded to prevent a false step while allowing explosive movement in the intended release direction.
records.fault_trigger: Swaying, rocking, or bouncing pre-snap rather than settling into a loaded position; or so rigid and locked that the first movement requires a reset. A false step at the snap is the downstream symptom.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Positional variance of Pelvis Center and the shoulder midpoint across the pre-snap frames - low variance indicates a settled stance, excessive variance indicates swaying or rocking. Requires a sequence of frames rather than a single static frame, so it needs the dynamic pipeline.
records.coaching_cue: Still but not stiff - loaded and ready to go.

records.name: WR - Standard - Stance - Weight Distribution
records.ideal_execution_standard: Approximately 70-80% of body weight is loaded onto the front leg. The rear leg remains available to contribute to the release. The receiver should be able to roll forward off the front foot without rocking backward or taking a false step.
records.fault_trigger: Weight sitting back on the rear leg or evenly split, forcing a backward rock or false step before the release.
records.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Horizontal position of the hip midpoint (Pelvis Center) relative to the front vs rear ankle - forward bias indicates front-leg loading. Approximate proxy for the 70-80% split; pose gives position, not force, so this is inferred from geometry rather than measured directly.
records.coaching_cue: Load the front leg - ready to roll, not rock.
